docs.text:
Shared interactive prompting helpers (category selection).

ask_category prefers questionary (arrow-key select + type-to-filter) when the dependency is installed; without it, it falls back to a plain rich prompt with silent validation — no category dump in the prompt.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Journal-native command mutations (roadmap step 6): every mutating command (add / edit / delete / fixes) builds a mutation, appends it to the canonical journal, and persists the checkpoint. There is no intermediate store: the journal IS the store of record, the ledger's engine owns balance chaining and date ordering, and ledger.json is the snapshot the next boot hydrates from.

Mutation ids are content hashes (one hash scheme end-to-end); machine paths stamp a monotonic ts so identical content still yields distinct ids (the Q8 lesson). Command failures happen BEFORE the append: a rejected command leaves no journal line, so every line records a change that actually happened.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Application configuration (categories, data location).

Personal configuration lives OUTSIDE the source tree: a TOML file at ~/.financials.toml (user level) and/or ./financials.toml (project level), loaded via clevis's cascade (project overrides user overrides defaults). None of those values are committed — the repo carries only generic defaults so the tool runs out-of-the-box anywhere.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Config-file loader (separate module so tests can patch it in isolation).

Thin wrapper around clevis.get_config with the CLI layer disabled — financials config comes from files and defaults only.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Confirm an open entry in one step (financials confirm).

The fast path for the view's OPEN section: a landed-but-unconfirmed expected row (e####) or rule instance (r:-hash) is committed into the journaled ledger with the zero-prompt idiom — the stored values are taken as-is, no field prompts. The adjust path stays 'edit ' (prefilled prompts); a wrong confirm is recoverable via delete/edit, and the commit is journaled either way.

Resolver chain (same shape as edit/delete, exact ids only): t#### (committed hash) -> already actual: idempotent no-op (exit 0) e#### (expected) -> ConfirmMutation retires the e-row and the actual lands in one mutation; the expected row is dropped only after the confirm applied r:-hash (rule instance) -> AddMutation with the rule's own values; a covering commit supersedes the instance automatically, a drifted one is excepted Bare 'confirm' shows the OPEN section (the confirmation backlog) and asks which row to confirm. Anything unresolvable exits 2 with the standard 'Onbekende id' message.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Delete an existing transaction or expected entry (financials delete).

Resolves the id in the committed ledger (hash id, full or unambiguous prefix) or the expected register (e####), shows the row, and requires an explicit confirmation (bare Enter is NOT yes). Actual rows are applied as one DeleteMutation carrying the victim's full pre-image (the engine verifies it against the live row and refuses loudly on mismatch). Expected rows are removed from the expected register (no balance chain).

There is no undo; the journal IS the audit trail of what was removed.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Edit an existing transaction or expected entry (financials edit).

Resolves the id in the committed ledger (hash id, full or unambiguous prefix) or the expected register (e####), then prompts Datum/ Omschrijving/Categorie/Bedrag pre-filled with the current values — Enter keeps the value. Actual rows are applied as one UpdateMutation (full replacement of the mutable fields; the id and linked references ride along; date moves re-insert with propagated balances) — the engine's update = delete + insert. Expected rows are edited in the expected register (no balance chain to replay); a landed expected row (date <= today) confirms into the ledger as a ConfirmMutation.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Entry of new transactions (financials add).

Two paths: - interactive: financials add walks through date/description/category/ amount and validates the typed balance against the projected one; - non-interactive: financials add --date=... --description=... --category=... --amount=... [--checking=...] [--dry-run] for scripted use.

Every new record is an AddMutation appended to the canonical journal and applied by the ledger's engine: balance chaining and date ordering are the engine's (date-positioned insert with propagation). The reported id is the mutation's content-hash id.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-off expected (future) entries (financials expect).

Expected entries live in their own store (data/expected.json), the non-recurring analogue of recurrences.json — separate from the actual transactions, composed at view time.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Change-set engine (roadmap step 6): apply reviewed fix files against the journaled ledger.

The change-set is an in-memory list of dicts (the internal contract); financials fix --file loads a JSON/TOML document and routes it through this engine. Field ops re-point at the committed ledger: each op becomes one UpdateMutation carrying the target's FINAL row state (idempotent, final-state semantics — the from-guard still prevents stale edits from clobbering newer values). remove_row emits a DeleteMutation targeting the victim's journal id (pre-image from the ledger). add_expected_row and e-targeted remove_row keep operating on the expected register (hypotheticals, overlay — never committed facts).

Every mutation is applied through the single write step (commands.append_and_apply): append → boot (replay) → checkpoint. A guard violation aborts BEFORE any append, so every journal line records a change that actually happened.

{ "fixes": [ {"id": "d9906804515c73c2", "field": "description", "from": "Terug", "to": "Terug: parking", "reason": "typo"}, {"id": "e0004", "op": "remove_row", "reason": "spurious"} ] }

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Groups: named rollups of projected/committed rows (financials group).

A group bundles related rows into one virtual row in the view — the credit-card statement case: every purchase of one statement is a member (e####, committed hash id, or r: rule instance) and the statement shows as a single "Mastercard" row with the summed amount on the payment date.

Groups are organization metadata, NOT money movement: they are not journaled (journal = committed money; expected + rules + groups = forecast inputs), they live in their own groups.json overlay, and membership edits never touch the member rows themselves. The projection is a VIEW: hiding members and rolling them up happens at render/walk time, and a group's members keep their ids — group add/remove only edits the membership list.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Journal (append-only mutations) + ledger (applied transactions).

Identity vs integrity (decided 2026-09-18, docs/journaled-ledger.md): - a MUTATION's id IS its anti-corruption validator: 16-hex content hash over the canonical mutation minus the id (rehash on read) - a TRANSACTION's id is assigned ONCE by its creating mutation (add | confirm) and never recomputed — updates and balance propagation keep it, so linked/retires never need scanning - a transaction carries a separate stored hash (content hash minus the hash field, balances included) guarding its row on disk; recomputed by every writer (insert, update, propagate) - identical mutation content needs distinct ids (two Q8 rows): every mutation carries ts (creation time, hashed content) so content hashes never collide between two real entries Ops: add | update | delete | confirm — no opening op (openings are ordinary add transactions; the first posting to an account creates it).

{"date": "2024-11-24", "description": "Opening", "category": "Inkomsten", "postings": {"checking": 2776.47}, "op": "add", "id": "c41fd0e93b6f871a"} {"date": "2024-11-24", "description": "Opening", "category": "Inkomsten", "postings": {"savings": 20000.0}, "op": "add", "id": "9e2ac1b0774410f3"} {"date": "2024-11-24", "description": "Huur", "category": "Inkomsten", "postings": {"checking": 350.0}, "op": "add", "id": "cb2214d53b6f871a"} ...

Composition per the design: committed ledger ⊕ expected one-offs ⊕ rule expansions. The projection is a VIEW: nothing here writes stores.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
CLI for recurring rules (financials recurrence) — phase 7.

The engine (recurrences.py) stays pure storage/expansion; this module is the command surface. Rules are the recurring analogue of the expected register — overlay/config, NOT journaled: the journal is the story of committed money only (owner decision, 2026-09-21).

Commands (wired in cli.py): recurrence list all rules + next projected instances recurrence add [...] create a rule (flags or prompted) recurrence pause/resume toggle a rule's active state recurrence remove delete a rule, with confirmation recurrence detect [--min N] propose rules from history (review only; add turns one into a rule)

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Recurring rules: storage, expansion, and superseding (financials recurrence).

Rules are NEVER materialized into the transaction store. They expand dynamically at view time into virtual expected instances for a period window; an instance is superseded (skipped) when a real transaction covers the same period — same category, amount within tolerance, within ± days of the rule's day-of-month.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Rich visual reports over data/transactions.json.

All flow figures exclude Overdracht (internal transfers between the owner's own accounts). Only actual rows are reported; the count of pending expected rows is shown as context.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
Quick-add shorthand parser for financials add "...".

Grammar (left to right, whitespace-separated): [date] [amount] [Category:]description

  • date: ISO (2026-09-12), vandaag/today, morgen/tomorrow, overmorgen, gisteren/yesterday, eergisteren, or ±Nd relative days (e.g. -3d). Relative days REQUIRE the d suffix — bare "-25" is always an amount.
  • amount: signed (+/-) or currency-marked (€/eur) number, comma decimal allowed, 0 rejected. A bare unsigned number is NEVER an amount — it stays part of the description ("25 jaar jubileum" keeps its text).
  • rest: description, optionally "Category: description" where Category case-insensitively matches an approved category.

Anything omitted is prompted afterwards by the caller (date defaults to today via Enter); nothing is ever silently assumed.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
The TUI's step-3 add dialog: a native Textual form (modal screen) for financials tui's a key.

One source of truth for the RULES: validation, projection and the save mutations are imported from the CLI modules (entry._validate / _validate_amount, commands.projected_checking / cmd_add, expected.add_expected) — only the PROMPTING is native widgets. The same dispatch as the CLI applies: a future date saves to the expected register instead of the journal (no balance chaining — expected rows have no balances), and the CLI's future-date rejection inside entry._validate is bypassed by dispatching BEFORE it (CLI parity: entry.add_transaction dispatches before _validate too).

Form: Datum / Omschrijving / Categorie / Bedrag / checking-saldo confirmation. Enter walks the fields (Tab works natively too); on the saldo field Enter submits. Esc cancels (dismiss(None)).

The category is a FUZZY AUTOCOMPLETE (textual-autocomplete), not free text: the approved categories (config-driven, call time) are offered in a dropdown the moment the field takes focus — an empty input shows ALL of them (questionary-style), typing narrows fuzzily. Enter completes the highlighted match and advances to the next field (the library intercepts Enter/Tab while the dropdown is visible; a mouse click completes too). Esc with the dropdown open only hides it — a second Esc cancels the dialog. Enter on a hidden dropdown accepts an EXACT approved category; anything else is refused inline (submit re-validates every value, so a Tab-past is caught at the gate too). A bare 'q' in any field cancels (CLI parity).

The saldo confirmation shows the live projection for the typed date+amount; blank accepts the projection (the data-quality gate is "you saw the number", the typed value is never stored — balances are engine-computed). Enter-driven — no per-keystroke ledger boots.

Tests: pilot-pressable. Validation errors render inline (a Static line) instead of rich console output.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
The TUI (steps 1–3): a scrollable ledger view — Textual App + DataTable, consuming build_view (the same composition as list; one composition, two renderers) — the step-2 readonly detail dialog, and the step-3 add dialog (a, implemented in tui/add.py).

Keys: up/down (j/k) move the row cursor one row; pageup/pagedown by page; home/end jump to the first/last row; q or escape quits; a opens the add dialog; enter opens the detail dialog on an entry row. The DataTable clamps at the first/last row by itself (no offset math here) and auto-scrolls the viewport when the cursor reaches a screen edge. The table holds the FULL committed history above the actuals window; the initial view is positioned on the projection: the PROJECTIE row at the bottom of the viewport with the 10 rows above it starting at the top, so the forecast's near future is what you see first.

Row design: every entry row is TWO lines tall — the Datum column holds the date; the merged second column holds the id (line 1, dim) and "description / category" (line 2); the amount and the two balances are their own single-line columns. Section separators stay one line (label in the merged column). The merged column FILLS: the other columns stay content-sized and it takes every remaining cell (fit_columns — DataTable has no flex columns), so the numbers end flush at the right edge. Rows are mixed-height (add_row height=2); only the initial-position scroll math needs line offsets — cursor, keys and dialogs stay row-based.

Step 2: Enter on an entry row opens the readonly DetailScreen (the row's full data + a provenance status line); Esc/q closes it. The screen composes from the entry tuple so the editable step reuses it.

Step 3: a opens the AddScreen form (native widgets; the validation and save rules are imported from the CLI modules). On save the table rebuilds from a fresh build_view and the cursor lands on the newly added row; a toast confirms the new id.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-time bootstrap for the journaled ledger (roadmap step 1).

See docs/journaled-ledger.md. Reads the current stores and emits, into a STAGING directory (default: /migration — never the live store root, never overwriting existing outputs without --force):

events.jsonl append-only journal: two opening events (seed balances, derived from the first row) + one committed event per actual row, in replay order; NO sequence numbers — the row order IS the order. id = 16-hex content hash over the canonical event minus id (self-validating, idempotent appends, deterministic bootstrap) ledger.json checkpoint: folded entries + computed balances + tip (id of the last journal event — the watermark) expected.json pruned hypotheticals (balances and source_line stripped) rules.json recurrences, carried as-is (they never had balances)

Seed rule (decided 2026-09-18): opening = first row's recorded balance minus that row's own effect on the account. Worked example t0001 (2024-11-24, Huur, +350,00, recorded 3.126,47 / 20.000,00): checking opening = 3126.47 - 350.00 = 2776.47 savings opening = 20000.00 (no transfer in the first row)

Op vocabulary (final): add | update | delete | confirm. No opening op (openings are ordinary add mutations: "Opening", Inkomsten); no reconcile op — money that moved without a transaction becomes an explicit correction TRANSACTION (owner policy 2026-09-18: "I will always create a transaction implementing the mutation"); the bootstrap derives those correction rows and lists them for review.

Every mutation carries ts (creation time, part of the hashed content): identical content then yields DISTINCT ids (two Q8 rows stay two rows — the 2026-09-19 duplicate-collapse incident). Machine-minted rows get a monotonic clock (never repeats); human entries rely on manual distinctness. Ids are minted through journal.py's Mutation classes, so bootstrap and engine share one hash scheme.

Verification gate (two-tier): HARD: the folded TIP must equal the recorded tip — the one comparison that validates the entire amount chain end-to-end. On failure: report, exit non-zero, write NOTHING. SOFT: per-row balance deviations are counted and shown; after the correction pass this must be EMPTY — any survivor is an inconsistency between corrections and the fold.

Run by the owner (Makefile target: migration-boostrap): uv run python scripts/bootstrap_journal.py

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-time cleanup: drop the 8 test-pollution rows from expected.json.

2026-09-21: runs of tests/test_edit_move.py before the expected-store isolation fix appended one expected row per run via the unpatched add_expected — the test's move signature (Terug / Uitgaven / -30.00 / today+10 / note "expected entry"). Live ids e0092–e0099 (8 runs). The promotion's drift guard correctly refused: these rows exist ONLY in the live store, absent from the bootstrap baseline.

This script removes ONLY rows matching the exact signature below; any row with the id but different content REFUSES the run (owner data is never guessed away). Backup before write; post-verify the store parses.

Run: uv run python scripts/drop_expected_pollution.py # report only uv run python scripts/drop_expected_pollution.py --write # backup + drop

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-time data promotion (roadmap step 6, phase D1–D6).

Moves the migration staging stores to their canonical locations and retires the old stores — renamed with a timestamp, never destroyed. After this, command_journal() resolves to /journal.jsonl (the staging file no longer exists) and the app boots from the promoted stores with no further change.

Moves (in order, rollback = copy the backups back): D1 data/journal.jsonl -> backups/journal.jsonl.retired- (old audit trail) D4 migration/journal.jsonl -> data/journal.jsonl (the event journal) migration/ledger.json -> data/ledger.json (its checkpoint) D2 data/transactions.json -> backups/transactions.json.retired- D3 data/expected.json -> backups/expected.json.retired- migration/expected.json -> data/expected.json (pruned baseline) D5 migration/rules.json deleted ONLY when byte-identical to data/recurrences.json (which stays put); refusal otherwise D6 migration/ removed when empty

Guards: - pre-flight: the staging journal folds cleanly and its tip is recorded; the same tip must hold after the move (the move is byte-preserving) - expected.json drift check: any row present in the LIVE store but missing from the staging baseline REFUSES the promotion loudly (rows added after the bootstrap would be lost) — the owner decides - post-verify: load_ledger() from the promoted location == the pre-flight fold (ids + balances)

Run (Makefile target: migration-promote): uv run python scripts/promote_stores.py # dry-run: report only uv run python scripts/promote_stores.py --write # backups + move + verify

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-time regeneration: rewrite the staging checkpoint to the canonical fold (roadmap step 6 boot requirement).

Why: the staged migration/ledger.json was written by the bootstrap's file-order evidence pass (step 1). Step 3 made the engine's date-positioned fold THE canonical fold (design note, 2026-09-21), so the staged checkpoint's ROW ORDER is stale wherever a journal row's date differs from its file position (the 47 known inversion rows). Balances are fine (tip holds: unchanged from the bootstrap) — only the order is stale, but load_ledger hydrates rows as persisted, so a stale order boots the ledger in non-date order until a tail replay re-derives it. This script folds the journal canonically and persists the result atomically.

Run (Makefile target: migration-recheckpoint): uv run python scripts/recheckpoint.py # dry-run: report only uv run python scripts/recheckpoint.py --write # backup + rewrite + verify

Verification gate: after writing, hydration from the new checkpoint must equal a fresh fold exactly (ids + balances), and the tip balances must hold at the bootstrap values.

docs.title: Docstring
docs.text:
One-time repair: re-mint stale mutation ids in the migration journal.

The step-2 observer bug (2026-09-19): four live confirm rows were appended by a writer that stamped ts into the journal line but minted the id over content WITHOUT ts. The id doubles as the row's anti-corruption validator (16-hex content hash over the canonical mutation minus the id), so those rows now fail fold()'s rehash verification — the fold refuses loudly.

This script scans the journal, re-derives the id from each mismatched row's own content (the content itself is never touched), and rewrites ONLY the affected lines. Everything else stays byte-identical.

Run (Makefile target: migration-remint): uv run python scripts/remint_journal_ids.py # dry-run: report only uv run python scripts/remint_journal_ids.py --write # backup + repair + verify

Verification gate: after writing, the full journal must fold cleanly (at the bootstrap tip balances); the script refuses to write when the scan finds nothing, and reports loudly when the post-fold check fails.

docs.title: What kind of application this is
docs.text: financials is a personal, journal-first personal-finance command-line application with a terminal UI: an append-only event-sourced money journal (component:journal-core) that every mutating command flows through (component:journal-native-command-mutations), with forecasting, grouping and reporting as projections on top — never as second stores of truth.

docs.title: Core concepts and where they live
docs.text:
Mutations vs transactions — identity vs integrity (concept:1). The journal stores mutations; their content-hash ids are rehash-verified on read, while a transaction's id is assigned once and never recomputed. The ledger is the fold of the journal (concept:2) — replay in append order into date-positioned transactions (business-rule:9) whose balances propagate forward; checkpoints serialize the fold, atomically (business-rule:6), and boot hydrates from checkpoint plus journal tail.

Committed versus forecast. Three stores divide the world: the journal is the only record of committed money (concept:7); the expected register holds strictly future one-off rows (concept:6); recurrence rules expand virtually, never materialized (concept:9, non-goal:2). The open/confirm boundary is the hinge: a landed row (concept:21) becomes actual through a single ConfirmMutation that both retires the expected row and lands the actual (concept:8, concept:20).

The typed id space (concept:22). t#### actual, e#### expected, g#### group, r:-hash rule instance — one id contract reused by edit, delete, confirm and group resolution (concept:27), with the resolver chain in business-rule:99 spanning all three member id families (concept:19).

One composition, three renderings (component:ledger-view-layer). The projection composes actuals + expected + rule expansions (business-rule:75) with group rollups (concept:17), then serves list, the TUI shell (component:tui-shell — history, OPEN and PROJECTIE as one table; business-rule:87) and the reporting layer (component:reporting-layer).

Interaction is prompted, bilingual, and abort-safe. The interactive add flow (component:interactive-add-flow) projects the new checking balance and makes the user acknowledge it (concept:15); the TUI add dialog (tui/add.py) reuses the CLI's validation rules rather than duplicating them; the shared category ask layer (component:ask-layer) and config layer (component:config-layer) define one approved-category list; every prompt loop aborts cleanly.

Migrations are events too. The maintenance scripts (component:maintenance-scripts) moved legacy stores into the journal with the same transparency: explicit corrections instead of hidden reconciling entries (concept:34, non-goal:8), staging plus fold-verification before any write, and the no-reconcile op discipline the journal keeps to this day.

docs.title: financials in one view
docs.text:
Scope. 75 modules, 26 components, 148 business-rules, 37 concepts, 7 processes, 9 non-goals, 11 surface commands — the analysis base this summary condenses (business-rules: deterministic sample of 50 of 148; all other payload families read in full).

Archetype. An append-only journal-first finance CLI with a terminal UI: committed money lives only in a content-hash-integrity journal folded into a date-positioned ledger; forecasts (expected register, recurrence rules, groups) are projections that never themselves move money.

Top capabilities. Three-mode quick add with balance-confirmation gate; one-step confirm of landed open rows (single retires-and-lands mutation); guided edit/delete across the full typed id space (t####/e####/g####/r:); virtual recurrence rules with human-gated detection; group rollups in the view only; a composed projection serving list, TUI and Rich reports with Overdracht-excluded flows.

Non-goals that shape it. No reconcile/account-creation ops — accounts emerge from postings and unexplained money is an explicit reviewed correction; rules never materialize; groups never journal; reporting never reconciles.

Start here. Read the product summary for capability-by-capability detail, then the archetype mapping for how the concepts live in the components; use financials list as the designated id source for anything edit/confirm/delete.

Verification status. 4 objections are recorded in the vault by the verification phase and remain open — none are resolved in this engagement; read them before treating any claim above as final.

docs.title: 3. Archetype mapping
docs.text:
Rendered from narrative:archetype-mapping-financials v12 (agent-authored, produced-under task:19; describes → 10 components: ask-layer, config-layer, expected-register-store, interactive-add-flow, journal-core, journal-native-command-mutations, ledger-view-layer, recurrence-rule-engine, reporting-layer, tui-shell; full incoming links executed on the narrative).

What kind of application this is. financials is a personal, journal-first personal-finance command-line application with a terminal UI: an append-only event-sourced money journal (component:journal-core) that every mutating command flows through (component:journal-native-command-mutations), with forecasting, grouping and reporting as projections on top — never as second stores of truth.

Mutations vs transactions — identity vs integrity (concept:1). The journal stores mutations; their content-hash ids are rehash-verified on read, while a transaction's id is assigned once and never recomputed. The ledger is the fold of the journal (concept:2) — replay in append order into date-positioned transactions (business-rule:9) whose balances propagate forward; checkpoints serialize the fold, atomically (business-rule:6), and boot hydrates from checkpoint plus journal tail.

Committed versus forecast. Three stores divide the world: the journal is the only record of committed money (concept:7); the expected register holds strictly future one-off rows (concept:6); recurrence rules expand virtually, never materialized (concept:9, non-goal:2). The open/confirm boundary is the hinge: a landed row (concept:21) becomes actual through a single ConfirmMutation that both retires the expected row and lands the actual (concept:8, concept:20).

The typed id space (concept:22). t#### actual, e#### expected, g#### group, r:-hash rule instance — one id contract reused by edit, delete, confirm and group resolution (concept:27), with the resolver in business-rule:99 spanning all three member id families (concept:19).

One composition, three renderings (component:ledger-view-layer). The projection composes actuals + expected + rule expansions (business-rule:75) with group rollups (concept:17), then serves list, the TUI shell (component:tui-shell — history, OPEN and PROJECTIE as one table; business-rule:87) and the reporting layer (component:reporting-layer).

Interaction is prompted, bilingual, and abort-safe. The interactive add flow (component:interactive-add-flow) projects the new checking balance and makes the user acknowledge it (concept:15); the TUI add dialog (tui/add.py) reuses the CLI's validation rules rather than duplicating them; the shared category ask layer (component:ask-layer) and config layer (component:config-layer) define one approved-category list; every prompt loop aborts cleanly.

Migrations are events too. The maintenance scripts (component:maintenance-scripts) moved legacy stores into the journal with the same transparency: explicit corrections instead of hidden reconciling entries (concept:34, non-goal:8), staging plus fold-verification before any write, and the no-reconcile op discipline the journal keeps to this day.

docs.title: 4. Product summary
docs.text:
Rendered from narrative:product-summary-financials v2 (kind: product-summary, audience: client, produced-under task:19). Structure and claims as captured; its business-rule basis was a deterministic sample of 50 of 148 business-rule facts.

One command surface, safety by default. Eleven subcommands (add, expect, edit, delete, confirm, group, recurrence, list, tui, report, fix) dispatch with no business logic in the dispatcher; Ctrl-C in any prompting command cancels cleanly ("Geannuleerd, nothing saved"); approved categories and data directory come from a two-level TOML cascade.

One-step confirmation. Bare confirm lists the OPEN section, then routes your id by shape (group / expected / rule instance / already-actual); an expected row commits only when landed and amount-bearing (business-rule:102).

Plan the future without moving money. The expected register (concept:6) keeps one-off future entries (e#### ids) in their own store, posting no balances; rows must be strictly future-dated and approved-category (business-rule:30), and future-dated add input routes there automatically.

Group the noise away. Groups roll related rows into one virtual view row, resolved across all three id families (business-rule:99); membership edits never move money or touch the ledger.

Record money in seconds. add runs three paths — flagged, quick-add one-liner, bare interactive — over one shared validator (business-rule:24); the shorthand (concept:23) reads date/amount/Category:description with bilingual day words and sign-or-euro money markers; future-dated complete entries go to the expected register instead of the journal.

Correct history with guides, not guesses. edit/delete resolve ids across the whole family chain with prefilled prompts and explicit typed confirmation ("ja" — bare Enter is never yes); un-grouping spares members; suppressing a rule occurrence keeps the rule running.

Every change is journal-native. Each command becomes one mutation through the single write step — timestamp, content-hash id, append, tail replay, checkpoint (business-rule:12); history is append-only and replayable.

See everything at once. The view composes committed history, actuals, OPEN, then PROJECTIE — expected entries plus virtual rule occurrences, visible until superseded by real rows or confirmed (business-rule:75) — one composition feeding list, the TUI shell and the report.

Let patterns propose; you decide. Recurrence rules expand virtually into the projection and detection only prints proposals — rule creation always requires the explicit seeded review loop.

Report the boundary-true record. Monthly overview, top-N category rankings, end-of-month balance curves in Dutch format; Overdracht transfers are excluded from flow totals but keep balance effects (business-rule:123).

Where the boundary lies. Rules never materialize into the ledger (non-goal:2); groups are never journaled; reporting never reconciles; the journal has no account registry and no reconcile op — unexplained money was materialized as explicitly reviewed correction transactions; maintenance and migration scripts report by default, back up before writing, and retire superseded stores as timestamped backups — never delete.

docs.title: 7. Core concepts
docs.text:
Concept census: 37. Read: 25 (deterministic id-sorted spread under the family cap; sample = first 5 ids 1,10,11,12,13 — census order 1,10,11,…,2,20 — then the executed set). Unread roll-call: concept:4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37. truncated: family > 25 — full rendering waits on fact-filter reads (S5 query grammar).

Id Term Definition (condensed) concept:1 identity vs integrity Mutation id = its anti-corruption validator (16-hex sha256 content hash, rehashed on read); Transaction id = identity assigned once by its creating mutation; separate stored hash guards the on-disk row concept:10 coverage window constants AMOUNT_TOLERANCE = 0.01, DAY_WINDOW = 5, RULE_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 35 — module-level literals composing coverage/lookback semantics concept:11 anchor row The chronologically last committed ledger row on or before today, whose balances seed the projection walk; None → project from a lookback before today concept:12 projection anchor The TUI's initial scroll position anchored on the PROJECTIE separator with a 10-line context window; computed in lines, not rows concept:13 entry kind Row provenance label in the detail dialog: KIND_COMMITTED "journaal-geboekt", KIND_OPEN "openstaand (geland, niet bevestigd)", KIND_PROJECTED "projectie (verwacht door regel)" concept:14 form-walk The add dialog's Enter-advances-focus discipline over the fixed field order Datum → Omschrijving → Categorie → Bedrag → checking-saldo; later-dependent state refreshed on Enter concept:15 saldo confirmation gate The fifth add field: user sees the live balance projection and must acknowledge it; typed value must match within a cent and is never stored; future date → expected-register marker concept:16 questionary-style autocomplete Full approved-category list offered the moment the field takes focus; typing narrows fuzzily (overridden should_show_dropdown/_handle_focus_change) concept:17 group rollup Virtual Transaction standing in for members at render/walk time (id g####, 📁 label (count), summed amount); view-time projection only concept:18 dangling member Group member id that no longer resolves through any id family or has a null amount; rendered in a dangling warning, excluded from the total concept:19 three id families Committed ledger hash ids, expected e#### ids, rule-instance r:-ids; groups resolve members uniformly across all three concept:2 fold Replaying the journal: each Mutation applied in append order, producing Transactions with propagated running balances; fold returns the ledger + tip hash and verifies the chain concept:20 ConfirmMutation The commit idiom where one mutation retires the open e-row and lands the actual (cmd_add with retires); failure keeps the e-row intact concept:21 landed An e#### with date ≤ today and an amount; the precondition making it confirmable (gates single-row and group confirm) concept:22 row-id scheme t#### actual, e#### expected, g####/prefix group, r:… rule instance; financials list is the documented id source concept:23 shorthand quick-add The positional shorthand [date] [amount] [Category:]description with Dutch relative/offset dates; missing fields prompted; help frames three input modes concept:24 action-style subcommand First positional chooses a sub-action dispatched by an if/elif ladder; actions live in a sibling module whose handlers return exit codes concept:25 exit-code dispatch contract Dispatch arm raises SystemExit with the handler's raw exit-code return; visualize-only commands exit 0. Under objection:1 (§19) — bare confirm rides a mutating arm, not a view arm concept:26 openstaand Dutch "outstanding": landed-but-uncommitted ledger content shown alongside actuals and projection concept:27 financials list as id source "Id from 'financials list'" is the documented provenance of every editable/deletable/confirmable id; omission offers the last 10 actual rows concept:28 expected register The one-off future-entries register behind expect (+ add auto-routing); --list shows, --remove takes e####, e#### confirm into the journal concept:29 signed amount Single signed float: positive = income, negative = expense — never magnitude + direction flag concept:3 tip (watermark) The id of the last APPLIED mutation in journal order; checkpoint persists {"tip", "entries"} so boot replays only the tail concept:30 reporting windows --top N categories; time window --months or --year (--year overrides), else whole period concept:31 cleanup-fixes journaling Reviewed fixes arrive as data/cleanup_fixes* (JSON/TOML), applied oldest-first with --all, journaled as .applied after application

docs.text:
Business-rule census: 148. Read/sample: 25 (deterministic id-sorted spread under the family cap; executed ids 1, 10, 11, 12, 100–120). Unread roll-call (compacted ranges): business-rule:2–9, 13–99, 121–148. truncated: family > 25 — full rendering waits on fact-filter reads (S5 query grammar). Rows in id order; anchors as captured.

Id Statement (condensed from payload) Anchors business-rule:1 Updating a transaction = delete followed by insert; the transaction's id rides along so linked references stay valid; balances re-derive through propagation of both steps src/financials/journal.py:227-235 business-rule:10 Checkpoint hydration does not re-fold: balances are first-class snapshot state; hydration rebuilds rows and verifies hash guards; bare bootstrap-era rows accepted; guard failures refused loudly src/financials/journal.py:158-175 business-rule:11 Inserting computes balances from the nearest parent dated on/before it, then propagates to every later transaction in ledger order, rehashing each — never cached stale src/financials/journal.py:206-225 business-rule:12 Every mutating command appends through append_and_apply — THE single write step: ts stamped when missing, id minted as content hash, journal append, boot via checkpoint + tail replay, converged checkpoint persisted src/financials/commands.py:72-85 business-rule:100 Rollup row: id = g####, emoji-flagged label with member count, member sum rounded to 2 decimals, status from first member, date = group date else members' max date src/financials/groups.py:184-189, 192-205 business-rule:101 Group ids minted g#### by scanning existing ids for highest numeric suffix + 1, zero-padded src/financials/groups.py:74-79 business-rule:102 Confirming an expected row refuses future-dated and amount-less rows (exit 2); only landed, amount-bearing rows commit src/financials/confirm.py:68-76 business-rule:103 A confirmed expected row commits as ONE ConfirmMutation (cmd_add retires=[e-id]); the e-row is dropped only after the commit applied — never before src/financials/confirm.py:44-61, 77-84 business-rule:104 Group confirm commits only LANDED members in (date, id) order; future/dangling/amount-less skipped with note; nothing confirmable exits 2; partial confirm exits 0 src/financials/confirm.py:125-131, 141-158 business-rule:105 After an e-member commits in a group confirm, membership re-points to the new committed id, reloading groups after every save src/financials/confirm.py:161-170 business-rule:106 A rule-instance member is skipped when an actual entry covers it (same category, checking posting within AMOUNT_TOLERANCE, date within DAY_WINDOW) — no double commits src/financials/confirm.py:181-192 business-rule:107 Confirm prefix-dispatches: g####→group, e####→expected (unknown→2), r:→rule instance; else ledger: already-actual no-op (0), unknown exit 2 src/financials/confirm.py:242-261 business-rule:108 A landed rule instance commits zero-prompt with the rule's OWN values and the occurrence date; a covering commit supersedes automatically src/financials/confirm.py:98-100, 114-121 business-rule:109 Invoking financials without a subcommand is an error — the parser requires one of the eleven registered subcommands; no default command src/financials/cli.py:23, 264 business-rule:110 A subcommand's exit code is its handler's return value: every dispatch arm ends in raise SystemExit(handler(...)) (except report, add-wrapped, and the list/tui view arms) src/financials/cli.py:264, 408 business-rule:111 Ctrl-C during any prompt-driven command is a clean cancel: add/edit/delete/confirm arms catch KeyboardInterrupt, print "Geannuleerd (Ctrl-C)", exit 0 src/financials/cli.py:288, 290, 307, 323 business-rule:112 fix requires an explicit target: neither --file nor --all is a parser error, never a silent no-op; --all applies pending cleanup_fixes* oldest-first, journaling as .applied src/financials/cli.py:264, 270 business-rule:113 group validates action args at dispatch: show/edit/delete need g####; add/remove need group + ≥1 row id; unknown action lists the seven allowed actions src/financials/cli.py:330, 362 business-rule:114 Both action-style subcommands default to list: financials group = group list, financials recurrence = recurrence list src/financials/cli.py:327, 374 business-rule:115 Five command modules import lazily inside their arm (ledger_view, confirm, groups, tui, recurrence_cli) so fast-path commands never pay for view/TUI/forecast imports src/financials/cli.py:272-372 (6 anchors) business-rule:116 The approved category set is config-driven — whatever FinancialsConfig.categories holds after the cascade, never hardcoded src/financials/config.py:58-60, model.py:48 business-rule:117 Configuration is cascade-only and cached: user TOML + optional project TOML over dataclass defaults; no CLI layer; single-session caching src/financials/config.py:42-48, config_loader.py:14-25 business-rule:118 Row ids are prefix-scoped: e resolves against the expected register ONLY; anything else against the actual register; failed expected-lookup returns None, no fall-through src/financials/model.py:98-116 business-rule:119 The expected register holds manual one-off future entries, persisted sorted by date, reads as empty list when absent src/financials/model.py:75-95, 22-24 business-rule:120 Source amounts are Dutch-locale euro strings: optional minus, '€' + space, '.' thousands, ',' decimals; '-€ 1.234,56' → -1234.56; else None src/financials/parsing.py:32, 46-59

docs.title: process:1 — Record an Actual Transaction
docs.text:
Trigger: user runs financials add with flags, a shorthand seed, or interactively for a transaction dated today or in the past. Enforces: business-rule:92.

process "Finance User"
  start "Transaction To Record"
  send "Run Add Command"
  receive "Read Outcome"
  end "User Informed"

process "Financials"
  start "Add Requested"
  service "Boot Ledger"
  exclusive "All Fields Provided?"
    if "No" goto "Prompt Missing Fields"
    else "Yes" goto "Future Date?"
  user "Prompt Missing Fields"
  exclusive "User Aborted?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Saved"
    else "No" goto "Future Date?"
  exclusive "Future Date?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Routed To Expected Register"
    else "No"
  service "Validate Against Ledger"
  exclusive "Validation Passed?"
    if "No" then
      end "Rejected Not Valid"
    else "Yes"
  service "Build AddMutation"
  service "Append Mutation And Checkpoint"
  end "Entry Saved"

message flows
  from "Finance User"."Run Add Command" to "Financials"."Add Requested" label "Add Request"
  from "Financials"."Entry Saved" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Recorded Balances"
  from "Financials"."Aborted Nothing Saved" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Abort Notice"
  from "Financials"."Rejected Not Valid" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Rejection Notice"

  user "Pick From Recent List"
  exclusive "Pick Cancelled?"

      end "Aborted Nothing Changed"
    else "No"
  service "Boot Ledger"
  service "Resolve Id In Ledger"
  exclusive "Committed Row?"
    if "Yes" goto "Edit Actual"
    else "No" goto "Expected Resolver"
  exclusive "Expected Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Expected Editor"
      end "Delegated"
    else "No" goto "Group Resolver"
  exclusive "Group Resolver"

      send "Delegate To Group Editor"

    else "No" goto "Rule Instance Resolver"
  exclusive "Rule Instance Resolver"

      send "Delegate To Occurrence Editor"
      end "Delegated Occurrence"
    else "No" goto "Resolve Or Refuse"

    if "Unknown" then
      end "Unknown Id"

docs.title: process:4 — Confirm an Open Entry
docs.text:
Trigger: user runs financials confirm <id> (or picks from the OPEN section) to turn a landed-but-unconfirmed entry into the ledger; bare confirm lists open rows. Enforces: business-rule:3.

process "Finance User"
  start "Confirmation Wanted"
  send "Run Confirm Command"
  receive "Read Outcome"
  end "User Informed"

process "Financials"
  start "Confirm Requested"
  exclusive "Id Provided?"
    if "No" goto "Show Open Section"
    else "Yes"
  user "Show Open Section"
  exclusive "Pick Made?"
    if "No" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Confirmed"
    else "Yes" goto "Route By Id Shape"
  exclusive "Route By Id Shape"
    if "Group Id" goto "Confirm Group Members"
    if "Expected Id" goto "Find Expected Row"
    if "Rule Instance Id" goto "Confirm Rule Instance"
    if "Committed Id" goto "Already Actual"
    else "Unknown" goto "Find Expected Row"
  service "Find Expected Row"
  exclusive "Expected Row Found?"
    if "No" then
      end "Unknown Id"
    else "Yes" goto "Guard Confirm Guards"
  exclusive "Guard Confirm Guards"
    if "Future Date" then
      end "Refused Still Future"
    if "Missing Amount" then
      end "Refused No Amount"
    else "Landed" goto "Apply Confirm Mutation"
  service "Apply Confirm Mutation"
  exclusive "Mutation Applied?"
    if "No" then
      end "Refused Not Applied"
    else "Yes" goto "Drop Expected Row"
  service "Drop Expected Row"
  end "Expected Confirmed"
  user "Confirm Group Members"
  end "Group Confirmed"
  service "Confirm Rule Instance"
  end "Instance Confirmed"
  service "Already Actual"
  end "No-Op Already Committed"

docs.title: 17. Data sensitivity
docs.text:
Sensitivity census: 18 — all rendered in full.

Id Statement (condensed) sensitivity:1 Boot-time corruption policy: content-hash mismatches refused loudly; truncation/reordering is NOT the hash's job — a tip absent from the journal refuses boot; failure direction always replayable (journal ahead of checkpoint) sensitivity:2 The projected checking balance shown in the add loop is the exact number the user must confirm (within 0.005); computed from the same date-positioned predecessor the engine fold chains from — any predecessor-selection drift would confirm a wrong balance sensitivity:3 _next_id reserves nothing: ids derive from highest existing eNNNN at load time — two concurrent adders can mint the same eNNNN and the remove path would delete both; single-user CLI assumed sensitivity:4 Overdracht bookings touch two accounts in one mutation; every interactive create/edit/move/delete of one warns about the savings chain; the change-set engine maintains the 'savings' = -amount mirror posting — any path forgetting the mirror silently corrupts the savings balance chain sensitivity:5 Coverage matching is year-gated: a covering transaction straddling a year boundary can never match across years, even though the ±5-day window itself crosses it sensitivity:6 The recurrence instance-commit path writes real money with NO typed confirmation gate (unlike remove/suppress which require 'ja') — an accidental Enter on the first prefilled question commits the booking sensitivity:7 open_rows is a view-level read walking the projection (writes nothing); code mutating through the view layer would corrupt the read-only contract shared by TUI and confirm sensitivity:8 fit_columns hand-sizes every column against the scrollable region: pinning content widths (Datum included), merged Transactie fills the rest minus cell padding so the render width exactly equals the viewport; break any term and columns visibly misalign sensitivity:9 The TUI bakes in project=0 and a projection horizon of Dec 31 of the current year; shifting these silently changes rendered rows and the anchored scroll position sensitivity:10 The TUI add dialog dispatches future-dated rows to add_expected BEFORE _validate — reordering _submit's steps pushes future rows into the journal path; the dispatch-before-validate ordering is load-bearing sensitivity:11 The TUI add screen imports the CLI's private validation internals as its rules source of truth; renames break the dialog silently at import time; rules must never be duplicated locally sensitivity:12 The last-resort member resolver re-expands rules over a wide window and re-hashes instance ids to match a dangling member — rule edits re-mint ids, so group membership silently references stale ids sensitivity:13 Group show excludes dangling members from the rollup total but lists them; all-dangling exits 2 — a stale membership degrades quietly into a wrong/empty total rather than failing loudly sensitivity:14 Group confirm mutates the membership file while iterating: reloads after every save and re-finds the group; an interrupted run leaves partially-confirmed state; the idempotent re-run path depends on the "is al actual" skip sensitivity:15 find_entry is a regression-sensitive resolver: an e-id once resolved to an actual row while remove routed by prefix, deleting the other store's row; the strict prefix scoping must not be relaxed sensitivity:16 APPROVED_CATEGORIES in model.py is computed once at import; ask._sorted_categories re-reads config per call — consumers must be consistent about their source of truth sensitivity:17 The report row filter matches "summary row" as a SUBSTRING of the note, so any note containing the phrase excludes a row from all flow figures and rankings — an over-matching exclusion sensitivity:18 Mutation ids are content hashes: repairing ids means rewriting immutable-looking journal rows in place — tooling assuming write-once rows must coordinate with the repair script (backup + fold verification)

docs.title: financials — what it does for its owner
docs.text:
One command surface, safety by default. Eleven subcommands (add, expect, edit, delete, confirm, group, recurrence, list, tui, report, fix) dispatch with no business logic in the dispatcher; Ctrl-C in any prompting command cancels cleanly ("Geannuleerd, nothing saved"); approved categories and data directory come from a two-level TOML cascade.

One-step confirmation. Bare confirm lists the OPEN section, then routes your id by shape (group / expected / rule instance / already-actual); an expected row commits only when landed and amount-bearing (business-rule:102).

Plan the future without moving money. The expected register (concept:6) keeps one-off future entries (e#### ids) in their own store, posting no balances; rows must be strictly future-dated and approved-category (business-rule:30), and future-dated add input routes there automatically.

Group the noise away. Groups roll related rows (a card statement's purchases) into one virtual view row, resolved across all three id families (business-rule:99); membership edits never move money or touch the ledger.

Record money in seconds. add runs three paths — flagged, quick-add one-liner, bare interactive — over one shared validator (business-rule:24); the shorthand (concept:23) reads date/amount/Category:description with bilingual day words and sign-or-euro money markers; future-dated complete entries go to the expected register instead of the journal.

Correct history with guides, not guesses. edit/delete resolve ids across the whole family chain (actual, expected, group, rule occurrence) with prefilled prompts and explicit typed confirmation ("ja" — bare Enter is never yes); un-grouping spares members; suppressing a rule occurrence keeps the rule running.

Every change is journal-native. Each command becomes one mutation through the single write step — timestamp, content-hash id, append, tail replay, checkpoint (business-rule:12); history is append-only and replayable.

See everything at once. The view composes committed history, actuals, OPEN, then PROJECTIE — expected entries plus virtual rule occurrences, visible until superseded by real rows or confirmed (business-rule:75) — one composition feeding list, the TUI shell and the report.

Let patterns propose; you decide. Recurrence rules expand virtually into the projection and detection only prints proposals — rule creation always requires the explicit seeded review loop.

Report the boundary-true record. Monthly overview, top-N category rankings, end-of-month balance curves in Dutch format; Overdracht transfers are excluded from flow totals but keep balance effects (business-rule:123).

Where the boundary lies. Rules never materialize into the ledger (non-goal:2); groups are never journaled; reporting never reconciles; the journal has no account registry and no reconcile op — unexplained money was materialized as explicitly reviewed correction transactions; maintenance and migration scripts report by default, back up before writing, and retire superseded stores as timestamped backups — never delete.

Business-rule scope: narrated from a deterministic sample of 50 of 148 business-rule facts (first five ids, then every third id to 138); concept, component, non-goal and process families were read in full.

docs.text: Anchored in the module docstring (src/financials/recurrences.py:1) and the virtual-synthesis body of expand_recurrences (src/financials/recurrences.py:147-182); virtual instances exist only in memory for views and confirmations.

docs.text: The recurrence CLI does not create rules automatically from detection — detection only prints proposals; rule creation always requires the explicit user approval of the seeded field loop (or fully-flagged add).

docs.text: The docstrings state it explicitly ('NOTHING is created'; 'the proposal alone never creates a rule') — recurring money movement is trusted only to a human-reviewed rule. Evidence anchors: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:855-857 and 915-918.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: The ledger TUI does no offset/scroll math for cursor movement or dialogs — the DataTable clamps at the first/last row and auto-scrolls the viewport itself by row; only the initial projection-anchor positioning uses line-based scroll math (rows are mixed-height, so that one case needs line offsets).

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Stated verbatim in the module docstring ('The DataTable clamps at the first/last row by itself (no offset math here)… only the initial-position scroll math needs line offsets') and honored by the code: _focus_row and _position_at are the only scroll computations, both called with call_after_refresh.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: Groups are not journaled and never move money: the projection hides members and rolls them up at render/walk time only, group add/remove edit only the membership list and leave the member rows untouched in their own stores.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Journal = committed money; expected + rules + groups = forecast inputs. Keeping groups outside the journal keeps the committed ledger authoritative and membership reversible.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: Confirm never commits a FUTURE rule instance itself: a future occurrence is handed to recurrence_cli's interactive prefilled prompt walk, and recurrence_cli's own future-date gate refuses an actual dated ahead of today — confirm does not bypass or duplicate that gate.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The module reuses recurrence_cli._confirm_instance for future instances (confirm.py:111-113) and its docstring states the gate belongs to recurrence_cli; keeping one date gate avoids two diverging validation paths.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: The reporting layer does no reconciliation or anomaly detection: it renders aggregated totals and balance curves as recorded; it never validates that summed flows match balance deltas (no flag-based or balance-mismatch logic lives in reporting).

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Balance-mismatch flags exist in the model (FLAG_BALANCE_CHECKING / FLAG_BALANCE_SAVINGS) but reporting only reads balances for display; checking is deferred to other layers.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: The journal op vocabulary deliberately has no reconcile operation (nor an opening op): money that moved without a transaction is never silently reconciled — it becomes an explicit correction transaction, listed for owner review.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Owner policy 2026-09-18: "I will always create a transaction implementing the mutation" — hidden reconciling entries would defeat the journal's auditability, so the maintenance tooling derives explicit correction rows instead.

docs.title: Non-Goal Statement
docs.text: The maintenance scripts do not silently destroy superseded data: retired stores are preserved (timestamped .retired backups), refused rows are always reported for owner decision, and nothing is ever guessed away.

"""Confirm an open entry in one step (financials confirm).

docs.title: Quirk Description
docs.text: remint() is a repair pass kept in the core module: it re-mints the ids of journal rows whose stored id no longer matches their content hash — a legacy of a 2026-09-19 writer bug where ts was written into the line but the id was minted before ts became hashed content (four live observer rows). Only affected lines are rewritten, byte-preserving the rest; a dry_run mode reports without writing. It exists so old journals stay foldable under the current hashing rules.

• src/financials/journal.py
# src/financials/journal.py — lines 413–446
def remint(source: Journal | Path | str, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
  """Re-mint the ids of rows whose stored id does not match their content
  hash (repair for the 2026-09-19 writer bug: ts was written into the
  line but the id was minted before ts was hashed content — four live
  observer rows).

  Only the affected lines are rewritten (byte-preserving everything
  else); the content itself is never touched — the id doubles as the
  anti-corruption validator, so a re-mint re-derives it from the row's
  own content. Returns the repaired rows as (line number, old id, new
  id). Dry-run reports without writing."""
  journal = source if isinstance(source, Journal) else Journal(source)
  path = journal.path
  lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
  repaired: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []
  for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
    if not line.strip():
      continue
    properties = json.loads(line)
    op = properties.pop("op", None)
    cls = Journal.MUTATIONS.get(op)
    if cls is None:
      raise NotImplementedError(f"mutation op {op!r} is not implemented")
    mutation = cls(**properties)
    if mutation.id and mutation.content_hash != mutation.id:
      new_id = mutation.content_hash
      properties["id"] = new_id
      properties["op"] = op
      ordered = {key: properties[key] for key in sorted(properties)}
      lines[number - 1] = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
      repaired.append((number, mutation.id, new_id))
  if repaired and not dry_run:
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
  return repaired

docs.title: Quirk Description
docs.text: _resolve_ledger_target matches a fix id as 'full hash id OR t.id.startswith(fix_id)' — a prefix match, not a word-boundary match. A fix id that is a prefix of another transaction's id does not merely risk ambiguity: _load_fixes_file and the fix-file format invite hand-written short ids, where full-hash vs short-prefix is indistinguishable. Ambiguity raises only when MORE THAN ONE row matches; a unique prefix silently wins, and a one-character prefix of a unique hash is a legal target.

# src/financials/fixes.py — lines 61–69
def _resolve_ledger_target(fix_id: str, ledger: Ledger) -> LedgerTransaction | None:
  """Resolve a fix's target in the committed ledger: full hash id or
  unambiguous prefix. Raises on ambiguity; None when absent."""
  if not fix_id:
    raise ValueError("fix has no id")
  matches = [t for t in ledger.transactions if t.id and (t.id == fix_id or t.id.startswith(fix_id))]
  if len(matches) > 1:
    raise ValueError(f"ambiguous id prefix in fix: {fix_id} ({len(matches)} matches)")
  return matches[0] if matches else None

# src/financials/ledger_view.py — lines 37–51
def command_journal() -> Journal:
  """The canonical journal. Promotion-aware: before the data promotion
  the migration staging journal is canonical (both files exist; the
  migration one holds the bootstrap chain); after promotion
  migration/journal.jsonl no longer exists and data/journal.jsonl is
  canonical. Resolved through fixes so tests can monkeypatch."""
  from financials.fixes import journal_file, migration_journal_file

  migration = migration_journal_file()
  if migration.exists():
    migration.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return Journal(migration)
  canonical = journal_file()
  canonical.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  return Journal(canonical)

def find_group(groups: list[Group], id_or_name: str) -> Group | None:
  """Exact id first, then unique id prefix, then the group NAME
  (case-insensitive exact, then unique case-insensitive prefix) —
  `group add Mastercard e0016` addresses the group by name. Ambiguous
  prefixes (two groups 'Mastercard september'/'Mastercard oktober') match
  nothing: ids stay the canonical address."""
  needle = (id_or_name or "").strip()
  if not needle:
    return None
  exact = next((g for g in groups if g.id == needle), None)
  if exact is not None:
    return exact
  hits = [g for g in groups if g.id.startswith(needle)]

def check_weekday(text: str) -> str:
  """Note when a date-shaped cell's weekday prefix contradicts the date
  ('' when consistent, or when the text is not date-shaped)."""
  match = DATE_RE.match(text.strip())
  if not match:
    return ""
  month = MONTHS.get(match.group("mon").lower())
  if month is None:
    return "unparsable month"
  try:
    actual = datetime.date(int(match.group("year")), month, int(match.group("day"))).strftime("%a")
  except ValueError:
    return "invalid calendar date"
  recorded = match.group("wd").capitalize()
  return "" if actual == recorded else f"weekday mismatch: recorded {recorded}, actual {actual}"

    return None
  console.print("[bold]Laatste 10 actuele rijen:[/bold]")
  for t in recent:
    console.print(
      f"  [dim]{t.id}[/dim]  {t.date}  {t.description}  [{t.category}]  {t.amount_eur:+,.2f}"
    )
  text = Prompt.ask("Id om te verwijderen (leeg = annuleren)", default="")
  return text.strip() or None

docs.title: Parity Relevance
docs.text: The two pickers can drift independently (e.g. different filters), so parity work should test bare 'edit' and bare 'delete' separately rather than assuming one shared recent-pick behavior.

docs.title: Quirk Description
docs.text: The canonical journal location (config-driven data_dir/journal.jsonl) is defined in fixes.py, and commands.py and ledger_view.py import it from there ('resolve the canonical journal through this module'). Before the data promotion, a migration staging journal shadows the canonical journal. The journal's home module is therefore the change-set engine — an odd home for a file every command touches.

# src/financials/fixes.py — lines 244–248
def journal_file() -> Path:
  """The canonical journal (config-driven location). Before the data
  promotion the migration staging journal shadows it (commands.py and
  ledger_view.py resolve the canonical journal through this module)."""
  return data_dir() / "journal.jsonl"

# src/financials/fixes.py — lines 270–272
# data_dir import kept at module bottom to avoid the circular import
# through commands (commands → fixes → commands).
from financials.config import data_dir  # noqa: E402  (module-level re-export)

docs.title: Parity Relevance
docs.text: Parity harnesses must resolve the journal path the same way (via fixes.journal_file), not hardcode data_dir/journal.jsonl, or the migration staging shadow will be missed.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
Scope. 75 modules, 26 components, 148 business-rules, 37 concepts, 7 processes, 9 non-goals, 11 surface commands — the analysis base this summary condenses (business-rules: deterministic sample of 50 of 148; all other payload families read in full).

Archetype. An append-only journal-first finance CLI with a terminal UI: committed money lives only in a content-hash-integrity journal folded into a date-positioned ledger; forecasts (expected register, recurrence rules, groups) are projections that never themselves move money.

Top capabilities. Three-mode quick add with balance-confirmation gate; one-step confirm of landed open rows (single retires-and-lands mutation); guided edit/delete across the full typed id space (t####/e####/g####/r:); virtual recurrence rules with human-gated detection; group rollups in the view only; a composed projection serving list, TUI and Rich reports with Overdracht-excluded flows.

Non-goals that shape it. No reconcile/account-creation ops — accounts emerge from postings and unexplained money is an explicit reviewed correction; rules never materialize; groups never journal; reporting never reconciles.

Start here. Read the product summary for capability-by-capability detail, then the archetype mapping for how the concepts live in the components; use financials list as the designated id source for anything edit/confirm/delete.

Verification status. 4 objections are recorded in the vault by the verification phase and remain open — none are resolved in this engagement; read them before treating any claim above as final.

docs.title: 3. Archetype Mapping
docs.text:
financials is a personal, journal-first personal-finance command-line application with a terminal UI: an append-only event-sourced money journal (component:journal-core) that every mutating command flows through (component:journal-native-command-mutations), with forecasting, grouping and reporting as projections on top — never as second stores of truth.

Mutations vs transactions — identity vs integrity (concept:1). The journal stores mutations; their content-hash ids are rehash-verified on read, while a transaction's id is assigned once and never recomputed. The ledger is the fold of the journal (concept:2) — replay in append order into date-positioned transactions (business-rule:9) whose balances propagate forward; checkpoints serialize the fold, atomically (business-rule:6), and boot hydrates from checkpoint plus journal tail.

Committed versus forecast. Three stores divide the world: the journal is the only record of committed money (concept:7); the expected register holds strictly future one-off rows (concept:6); recurrence rules expand virtually, never materialized (concept:9, non-goal:2). The open/confirm boundary is the hinge: a landed row (concept:21) becomes actual through a single ConfirmMutation that both retires the expected row and lands the actual (concept:8, concept:20).

The typed id space (concept:22). t#### actual, e#### expected, g#### group, r:-hash rule instance — one id contract reused by edit, delete, confirm and group resolution (concept:27), with the resolver chain in business-rule:99 spanning all three member id families (concept:19).

One composition, three renderings (component:ledger-view-layer). The projection composes actuals + expected + rule expansions (business-rule:75) with group rollups (concept:17), then serves list, the TUI shell (component:tui-shell — history, OPEN and PROJECTIE as one table; business-rule:87) and the reporting layer (component:reporting-layer).

Interaction is prompted, bilingual, and abort-safe. The interactive add flow (component:interactive-add-flow) projects the new checking balance and makes the user acknowledge it (concept:15); the TUI add dialog (tui/add.py) reuses the CLI's validation rules rather than duplicating them; the shared category ask layer (component:ask-layer) and config layer (component:config-layer) define one approved-category list; every prompt loop aborts cleanly.

Migrations are events too. The maintenance scripts (component:maintenance-scripts) moved legacy stores into the journal with the same transparency: explicit corrections instead of hidden reconciling entries (concept:34, non-goal:8), staging plus fold-verification before any write, and the no-reconcile op discipline the journal keeps to this day.

docs.title: 4. Product Summary
docs.text:
One command surface, safety by default. Eleven subcommands (add, expect, edit, delete, confirm, group, recurrence, list, tui, report, fix) dispatch with no business logic in the dispatcher; Ctrl-C in any prompting command cancels cleanly ("Geannuleerd, nothing saved"); approved categories and data directory come from a two-level TOML cascade.

One-step confirmation. Bare confirm lists the OPEN section, then routes your id by shape (group / expected / rule instance / already-actual); an expected row commits only when landed and amount-bearing (business-rule:102).

Plan the future without moving money. The expected register (concept:6) keeps one-off future entries (e#### ids) in their own store, posting no balances; rows must be strictly future-dated and approved-category (business-rule:30), and future-dated add input routes there automatically.

Group the noise away. Groups roll related rows (a card statement's purchases) into one virtual view row, resolved across all three id families (business-rule:99); membership edits never move money or touch the ledger.

Record money in seconds. add runs three paths — flagged, quick-add one-liner, bare interactive — over one shared validator (business-rule:24); the shorthand (concept:23) reads date/amount/Category:description with bilingual day words and sign-or-euro money markers; future-dated complete entries go to the expected register instead of the journal.

Correct history with guides, not guesses. edit/delete resolve ids across the whole family chain (actual, expected, group, rule occurrence) with prefilled prompts and explicit typed confirmation ("ja" — bare Enter is never yes); un-grouping spares members; suppressing a rule occurrence keeps the rule running.

Every change is journal-native. Each command becomes one mutation through the single write step — timestamp, content-hash id, append, tail replay, checkpoint (business-rule:12); history is append-only and replayable.

See everything at once. The view composes committed history, actuals, OPEN, then PROJECTIE — expected entries plus virtual rule occurrences, visible until superseded by real rows or confirmed (business-rule:75) — one composition feeding list, the TUI shell and the report.

Let patterns propose; you decide. Recurrence rules expand virtually into the projection and detection only prints proposals — rule creation always requires the explicit seeded review loop.

Report the boundary-true record. Monthly overview, top-N category rankings, end-of-month balance curves in Dutch format; Overdracht transfers are excluded from flow totals but keep balance effects (business-rule:123).

Where the boundary lies. Rules never materialize into the ledger (non-goal:2); groups are never journaled; reporting never reconciles; the journal has no account registry and no reconcile op — unexplained money was materialized as explicitly reviewed correction transactions; maintenance and migration scripts report by default, back up before writing, and retire superseded stores as timestamped backups — never delete.

Business-rule scope: narrated from a deterministic sample of 50 of 148 business-rule facts (first five ids, then every third id to 138); concept, component, non-goal and process families were read in full.

docs.title: Component: ask-layer
docs.text: Shared interactive category-prompting: ask_category returns one approved category, preferring questionary (arrow-key select + type-to-filter, j/k keys disabled because they conflict with the filter) when that package is importable, else a plain rich Prompt fallback with RETRY_LIMIT silent validation; both paths return the ABORT sentinel on user cancel. grounded in: file:src/financials/ask.py, task:15

docs.title: Component: Change-set fix engine
docs.text: Roadmap step 6 engine that applies reviewed fix files (change-sets) against the journaled ledger. THE single write path to the ledger: every op becomes a mutation appended via commands.append_and_apply (append → boot replay → checkpoint), so a guard violation aborts before any append and every journal line records a change that actually happened. apply_ops handles row ops (remove_row on ledger targets or e#### entries in the expected register, add_expected_row), apply_field_ops handles id+field+from+to fixes (each one from-guarded UpdateMutation with the final row state). apply_fixes loads a JSON fix file, dispatches to both, and runs the migration journal when one is present. grounded in: file:src/financials/fixes.py, task:6

docs.title: Component: checkpoint-regenerator
docs.text: One-time script that rewrites the migration staging checkpoint (migration/ledger.json) to the canonical fold of the staging journal. Dry-run folds the journal, prints tip balances, and diffs the existing checkpoint's entry ids against the fold's entry ids (reporting the first divergence row); --write backs up the checkpoint, regenerates it via financials.journal.checkpoint (atomic write), then verifies by hydrating from the rewritten checkpoint and comparing it exactly (ids + balances) to a fresh fold. grounded in: file:scripts/recheckpoint.py, subsystem:maintenance-scripts, task:16

docs.title: Component: CLI dispatcher
docs.text: The command-line entry of financials: one argparse main() that registers eleven subcommands (fix, report, add, expect, edit, delete, confirm, group, list, tui, recurrence), parses argv, and dispatches each command to a functional module (entry, expected, edit, delete, fixes, reporting, confirm, groups, ledger_view, tui, recurrence_cli). The module contains no business logic of its own: it translates arguments, delegates, and turns each handler's return value into the process exit code via raise SystemExit(handler(...)), while wrapping the four prompt-driven commands (add/edit/delete/confirm) in KeyboardInterrupt cancellation. Reached via the console-script entry point and the module main-guard (if name == "main": main()). grounded in: file:src/financials/cli.py, task:14

docs.title: Component: config-layer
docs.text: Runtime configuration for financials: a FinancialsConfig dataclass whose categories and data_dir are loaded from the clevis TOML cascade (user ~/.financials.toml + optional project ./financials.toml, no CLI layer), reached only through the cached accessor get_config(); exposes approved_categories() and expanduser'd data_dir(). The loader is isolated in config_loader.py specifically so tests can patch it in isolation. grounded in: file:src/financials/config.py, file:src/financials/config_loader.py, task:15

docs.title: Component: Confirm command
docs.text: The one-step confirmation fast path for landed-but-unconfirmed entries: bare confirm shows the ledger's OPEN section and asks which id to confirm; an id is then dispatched by prefix (g#### group / e#### expected row / r:-hash rule instance / otherwise a committed actual, which is a no-op). Expected rows commit zero-prompt via the ConfirmMutation path (cmd_add with retires, then the expected row is dropped) — the same path as edit's all-Enter confirm. Rule instances commit zero-prompt with the rule's own values when landed, or fall back to the interactive prefilled prompts when still future. Groups confirm every landed member in (date, id) order and re-point each retired e#### to its new committed id so the group survives. Exit codes: 0 confirmed/already-actual, 2 refused or nothing to do. grounded in: file:src/financials/confirm.py, task:13

docs.title: Component: expected-pollution-cleaner
docs.text: One-time cleanup script (2026-09-21) that removes the test-pollution rows that runs of tests/test_edit_move.py bled into the live expected.json. Rows are dropped only when both their id (e0092..e0099) and their content signature match exactly; matching is report-only until --write is passed, and expected.json is backed up before any write. grounded in: file:scripts/drop_expected_pollution.py, subsystem:maintenance-scripts, task:16

docs.title: Component: Expected-register store
docs.text: src/financials/expected.py manages one-off future entries in their own store (data/expected.json), separate from the journal: add_expected validates (must be future-dated, approved category, non-zero amount) and saves a STATUS_EXPECTED Transaction with eNNNN ids; fix files can re-create rows via add_expected_row_from_fix; list/remove round out the register CRUD. No balance posting happens here — balances start None until a confirmation retires the row into the ledger. grounded in: file:src/financials/expected.py, task:5

docs.title: Component: groups & rollups engine
docs.text: Named rollups of projected/committed rows (financials group): a group bundles related rows (credit-card statement purchases) into one virtual row in the view — members are e####, committed hash ids, or r: rule instance ids, and the statement shows as a single row with the summed amount on the rollup date. The module owns the Group dataclass, the groups.json overlay store, member-id resolution across the three id families, rollup-row construction, and the group CLI verbs (create/ add/remove/delete/edit/list/show). grounded in: file:src/financials/groups.py, task:12

docs.title: Component: Interactive add flow
docs.text:
src/financials/entry.py implements financials add's three entry paths — fully flagged, shorthand-seeded, and fully interactive — with a shared validator (validate) and an interactive prompt loop (_prompt) that pre-fills from a parsed Shorthand, projects the new checking balance from the ledger's date-positioned predecessor, and verifies the user's balance confirmation against that projection with a 3-attempt retry limit. Future-dated full entries are date-based dispatched into the expected register (add_expected). _grounded in: file:src/financials/entry.py, task:5
