docs.title: Concept: identity vs integrity
docs.text: Two distinct id roles in the journal (decdocs/journaled-ledger.md, 2026-09-18): a MUTATION's id IS its anti-corruption validator — a 16-hex sha256 content hash over the canonical mutation minus the id (rehashed on read). A TRANSACTION's id instead is identity, assigned ONCE by its creating mutation (add|confirm) and never recomputed; updates and balance propagation keep it, so linked/retired transactions never need rescanning. A transaction additionally carries a separate stored hash (content minus the hash field, balances included) that guards its row on disk.

docs.title: Concept: coverage window constants
docs.text: Window constants in the recurrences prelude compose the coverage/lookback semantics: AMOUNT_TOLERANCE = 0.01 (coverage amount match), DAY_WINDOW = 5 (days around the rule day that a covering transaction may sit), RULE_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 35 (the view's grace lookback before the ledger's anchor). All three are module-level literals consumed as literals by expansion and view code.

docs.title: Concept: anchor row
docs.text: The chronologically last committed ledger row on or before today, chosen by the chain-tip convention, whose calculated balances (checking and savings) seed the projection walk; when no committed row exists on or before today the anchor is None and balances project from a lookback before today instead.

docs.title: Concept: projection anchor
docs.text: The initial scroll position of the TUI ledger, anchored on the PROJECTIE separator row: that row lands at the bottom of the viewport with a fixed 10-line context window above it (_ANCHOR_CONTEXT_LINES), snapped so the top visible row is never cut mid-row. Because entry rows are two lines tall, the scroll offset is computed in LINES (summed per-row heights) not rows; only this initial positioning uses line math — cursor, keys and dialogs stay row-based.

docs.title: Concept: entry kind
docs.text: The row's provenance label shown in the detail dialog's status line — where the entry came from in the view's composition: KIND_COMMITTED "journaal-geboekt" (history band or actuals window), KIND_OPEN "openstaand (geland, niet bevestigd)", KIND_PROJECTED "projectie (verwacht door regel)". Kept as parallel per-entry state (_entries maps id → (entry, checking, savings, kind)).

docs.title: Concept: form-walk
docs.text: The add dialog's navigation discipline: Enter (or completing the category dropdown) advances focus through the fixed field order Datum → Omschrijving → Categorie → Bedrag → checking-saldo; on the last field (saldo) Enter submits the form. Tab also works natively. Later-dependent state (the saldo projection) is refreshed on Enter for the date and amount fields before advancing.

docs.title: Concept: saldo confirmation gate
docs.text: The fifth add-form field (Checking-saldo): the user is shown the live projection of the checking balance for the typed date+amount and must acknowledge it. Blank accepts the projection; a typed value must match it within a cent. The gate is "you saw the number" — the typed value is never stored. When no predecessor row exists there is no projection and the gate is skipped. On a future date the field instead carries the expected-register marker (no balance chaining).

docs.title: Concept: questionary-style autocomplete
docs.text: The category dropdown behavior the add dialog mimics from questionary: the FULL approved-category list is offered the moment the field takes focus (an empty input shows all candidates), typing narrows fuzzily. Implemented by overriding both should_show_dropdown (visible whenever any candidate exists, not only on a non-empty search string) and _handle_focus_change (focus alone routes through _handle_target_update to align + rebuild + show; blur hides).

docs.title: Concept: group rollup
docs.text: A virtual Transaction standing in for a group's members at render/walk time in the ledger view: members are hidden and replaced by one row (id g####, description 📁 label (count), amount = member sum) — a view-time projection only, member rows keep their own ids and stores.

docs.title: Concept: dangling member
docs.text:
A group member id that no longer resolves through any id family (resolve_member returns None) or has a null amount: the group show renders it in a dedicated dangling warning and excludes it from the total.

docs.title: business-rule:1
docs.text:
Updating a transaction is composed as delete followed by insert: the transaction's id (assigned at creation) rides along so linked references elsewhere stay valid, and balances re-derive through the propagation of both steps.

implemented in: src/financials/journal.py:227-235

docs.title: business-rule:10
docs.text:
Checkpoint hydration does not re-fold: balances are first-class snapshot state carried by the rows; hydration rebuilds transactions from the rows and verifies only their hash guards. Bare rows from bootstrap-era checkpoints (no hash guard) are accepted; guarded rows failing verify() are refused loudly.

implemented in: src/financials/journal.py:158-175

docs.title: business-rule:100
docs.text:
The rollup row for a group has id = the group id (g####), description formatted as an emoji-flagged label with the member count, amount = the member sum rounded to 2 decimals, status inherited from the first member row, and its rollup date is the group's own ISO date when set, else the members' max date.

implemented in: src/financials/groups.py:184-189, src/financials/groups.py:192-205

docs.title: business-rule:101
docs.text:
Group ids are minted as g#### by scanning all existing groups for ids matching g + digits and taking the highest numeric suffix plus 1, zero-padded to four places.

implemented in: src/financials/groups.py:74-79

docs.title: business-rule:102
docs.text:
Confirming an expected row refuses a row dated in the future and refuses a row with no amount (exit 2, nothing applied); only a landed, amount-bearing row commits.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:68-76

docs.title: business-rule:103
docs.text:
A confirmed expected row commits as one ConfirmMutation (cmd_add with retires=[e-row id]) and the expected row is dropped from the expected store only after the commit applied — never before.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:44-61, src/financials/confirm.py:77-84

docs.title: business-rule:104
docs.text:
Confirming a group id confirms only LANDED members (resolveable, not future, not already actual, amount-bearing) in (date, id) order; future, dangling and amount-less members are skipped with a note and the group survives; nothing confirmable exits 2, a partial confirm still exits 0.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:125-131, src/financials/confirm.py:141-158

docs.title: business-rule:105
docs.text:
After an e#### member commits inside a group confirm, the membership list is re-pointed from the retired e-id to the new committed hash id, reloading the group file after every save because resolve_member reboots the journal.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:161-170

docs.title: business-rule:106
docs.text:
A rule-instance member within a group confirm is skipped when an existing actual ledger entry already covers it — same category, a checking posting within AMOUNT_TOLERANCE of the rule amount, and a date within DAY_WINDOW of the occurrence — preventing double commits of superseded instances.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:181-192

docs.title: business-rule:107
docs.text:
Confirming an id prefix-dispatches: g#### with digits → group confirm, e#### with digits → expected-row confirm (unknown id → exit 2), r:-prefixed → rule-instance confirm; anything else resolves against the committed ledger where an already-actual entry is a no-op (exit 0) and an unknown id exits 2.

implemented in: src/financials/confirm.py:242-261

docs.title: Process: Record an Actual Transaction
docs.text:
Trigger: User runs financials add with flags, a shorthand seed, or interactively to record a transaction dated today or in the past

process "Finance User"
  start "Transaction To Record"
  send "Run Add Command"
  receive "Read Outcome"
  end "User Informed"

process "Financials"
  start "Add Requested"
  service "Boot Ledger"
  exclusive "All Fields Provided?"
    if "No" goto "Prompt Missing Fields"
    else "Yes" goto "Future Date?"
  user "Prompt Missing Fields"
  exclusive "User Aborted?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Saved"
    else "No" goto "Future Date?"
  exclusive "Future Date?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Routed To Expected Register"
    else "No"
  service "Validate Against Ledger"
  exclusive "Validation Passed?"
    if "No" then
      end "Rejected Not Valid"
    else "Yes"
  service "Build AddMutation"
  service "Append Mutation And Checkpoint"
  end "Entry Saved"

message flows
  from "Finance User"."Run Add Command" to "Financials"."Add Requested" label "Add Request"
  from "Financials"."Entry Saved" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Recorded Balances"
  from "Financials"."Aborted Nothing Saved" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Abort Notice"
  from "Financials"."Rejected Not Valid" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Rejection Notice"

docs.title: Process: Edit a Committed Transaction
docs.text:
Trigger: User runs financials edit <id> (or picks from a recent list) to change an existing entry; id resolvers fan out to expected entries, groups, and recurrence rule instances

process "Finance User"
  start "Change Wanted"
  send "Run Edit Command"
  receive "Read Outcome"
  end "User Informed"

process "Financials"
  start "Edit Requested"
  exclusive "Id Provided?"
    if "No" goto "Pick From Recent List"
    else "Yes"
  user "Pick From Recent List"
  exclusive "Pick Cancelled?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Changed"
    else "No"
  service "Boot Ledger"
  service "Resolve Id In Ledger"
  exclusive "Committed Row?"
    if "Yes" goto "Edit Actual"
    else "No" goto "Expected Resolver"
  exclusive "Expected Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Expected Editor"
      end "Delegated"
    else "No" goto "Group Resolver"
  exclusive "Group Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Group Editor"
      end "Delegated Group"
    else "No" goto "Rule Instance Resolver"
  exclusive "Rule Instance Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Occurrence Editor"
      end "Delegated Occurrence"
    else "No" goto "Resolve Or Refuse"
  exclusive "Resolve Or Refuse"
    if "Unknown" then
      end "Unknown Id"
    else "Committed Actual" goto "Edit Actual"
  user "Edit Actual"
  exclusive "Changes Collected?"
    if "Aborted" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Changed Two"
    if "No Changes" then
      end "No-Op Nothing To Save"
    else "Yes"
  exclusive "Future Date?"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Move-To-Expected"
      end "Delegated Move"
    else "No"
  service "Build UpdateMutation"
  service "Append Mutation And Checkpoint"
  end "Entry Updated"

message flows
  from "Finance User"."Run Edit Command" to "Financials"."Edit Requested" label "Edit Request"
  from "Financials"."Entry Updated" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Updated Balances"
  from "Financials"."Aborted Nothing Changed" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Abort Notice"
  from "Financials"."Aborted Nothing Changed Two" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Abort Notice Two"
  from "Financials"."No-Op Nothing To Save" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "No-Op Notice"
  from "Financials"."Delegated" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Delegation Notice"
  from "Financials"."Delegated Group" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Delegation Group Notice"
  from "Financials"."Delegated Occurrence" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Delegation Occurrence Notice"
  from "Financials"."Unknown Id" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Unknown Id Notice"
  from "Financials"."Delegated Move" to "Finance User"."Read Outcome" label "Moved Notice"

docs.title: Process: Delete a Committed Transaction
docs.text:
Trigger: User runs financials delete <id> (or picks from a recent list) to remove an existing entry, with confirmation; resolvers fan out to expected entries, groups, and recurrence rule instances

process "Finance User"
  start "Deletion Wanted"
  send "Run Delete Command"
  receive "Read Outcome"
  end "User Informed"

process "Financials"
  start "Delete Requested"
  exclusive "Id Provided?"
    if "No" goto "Pick From Recent List"
    else "Yes"
  user "Pick From Recent List"
  exclusive "Pick Cancelled?"
    if "Yes" then
      end "Aborted Nothing Deleted"
    else "No"
  service "Load Ledger And Resolve Id"
  exclusive "Committed Row?"
    if "Yes" goto "Delete Actual"
    else "No" goto "Expected Resolver"
  exclusive "Expected Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Expected Deleter"
      end "Delegated"
    else "No" goto "Group Resolver"
  exclusive "Group Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Group Deleter"
      end "Delegated Group"
    else "No" goto "Rule Instance Resolver"
  exclusive "Rule Instance Resolver"
    if "Yes" then
      send "Delegate To Occurrence Suppressor"
      end "Occurrence Suppressed"
    else "No" goto "Resolve Or Refuse"
  exclusive "Resolve Or Refuse"
    if "Unknown" then
      end "Unknown Id"
    else "Committed Actual" goto "Delete Actual"
  user "Delete Actual"

docs.title: Convention: convention:1
docs.text:
All content hashing goes through one frozen canonicalization: JSON with sorted keys, compact separators ("," and ":"), non-ASCII kept verbatim (ensure_ascii=False), and every float amount rounded to 2 decimals recursively before serialization.

applied in: src/financials/journal.py:40-54

docs.title: Convention: convention:10
docs.text:
Transaction rows keep raw and canonical category fields in parallel: category_raw/subcategory_raw preserve exactly what was found in the source, never modified, while category/subcategory are the canonical values and equal the raw ones right after import.

applied in: src/financials/model.py:61-64

docs.title: Convention: convention:11
docs.text:
Raw TSV category cells may carry a subcategory after a colon ('Sport: Lopen, Snowworld'); split_category partitions on ':' and returns (category, subcategory) with both parts stripped.

applied in: src/financials/parsing.py:62-68

docs.title: Convention: convention:12
docs.text:
Report tables use consistent Dutch column naming (Maand, Inkomsten, Uitgaven, Netto, Eind checking, Eind spaar, Aandeel, Gemiddeld) and box.SIMPLE; missing balance renders as an em-dash placeholder.

applied in: src/financials/reporting.py:102-111, src/financials/reporting.py:115-116

docs.title: Convention: convention:2
docs.text:
Add-flow exit codes are a 0/2 convention across the entry modules: 0 on success (including dry-run previews), 2 on any rejection, invalid input, or user abort ('q' or empty category pick) — nothing is ever partially stored on those paths ('Geannuleerd — niets opgeslagen' / 'Niet opgeslagen: …').

applied in: src/financials/entry.py:196, src/financials/entry.py:203-204, src/financials/entry.py:240-242, src/financials/entry.py:256-259, src/financials/entry.py:276-278

docs.title: Convention: convention:3
docs.text:
Re-export-by-delegation for patchability: entry.command_journal is a module-level delegating function (delegates to commands.command_journal) defined as a module attribute precisely so tests can patch financials.entry.command_journal directly; the same monkeypatch-friendly indirection runs through fixes for journal resolution in commands and entry (_boot).

applied in: src/financials/entry.py:34-35, src/financials/entry.py:49-52

docs.title: Convention: convention:4
docs.text:
Interactive amount prompts in edit.py accept a signed decimal (positive = income, negative = expenses), tolerate a comma as decimal separator ('5,25' → 5.25) by replacing ',' with '.' before float(), and round every entered value to 2 decimals. A zero is rejected unless the row is an expected row (0 is a legal placeholder there — reserve the entry now, fill in the amount when it lands). Failed attempts retry up to RETRY_LIMIT (3) times, then abort with None.

applied in: src/financials/edit.py:45-63

docs.title: Convention: convention:5
docs.text:
Recurrence rules persist as JSON via load_recurrences/save_recurrences, defaulting to the path returned by financials.model.recurrences_file; loading returns an empty list when the file is absent, and saving creates parent directories, serializes with ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, and a trailing newline. Both functions accept an optional explicit path so tests can redirect storage.

applied in: src/financials/recurrences.py:40-53

docs.title: Convention: convention:6
docs.text:
In recurrence_cli.py, 'today' is obtained only through the module-level TODAY() indirection function (returning date.today()) rather than calling date.today() inline — an explicit seam so tests can monkeypatch TODAY.

applied in: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:95-97, src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:75-84

docs.title: Convention: convention:7
docs.text:
Mutating a rule's exceptions after a fresh load_recurrences() never matches by object identity (rule is rule_hit) but by CONTENT (same description AND category): the scan's list is a different load, so identity would never fire. This content-match discipline appears in the drifted-commit exception path and the occurrence suppress path (and deliberately touches every rule sharing that description+category).

applied in: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:796-806, src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:837-843

docs.title: non-goal:1
docs.text:
Statement: The journal has no opening op: opening balances are represented as ordinary add transactions, and the first posting to an account implicitly creates the account — there is no separate account registry or account-creation step in the journal core (module docstring, src/financials/journal.py lines 23-24).

Rationale: Stated in the module docstring; accounts are an emergent property of postings rather than first-class objects.

docs.title: non-goal:2
docs.text: Statement: Recurrence rules are never materialized into the ledger: the module docstring states this design invariant, and expand_recurrences realizes it by synthesizing ephemeral virtual Transaction objects with status "expected" at expansion time rather than writing recurrence rows into stored ledger data. Rationale: Anchored in the module docstring (src/financials/recurrences.py:1) and the virtual-synthesis body of expand_recurrences (src/financials/recurrences.py:147-182); virtual instances exist only in memory for views and confirmations.

docs.title: non-goal:3
docs.text:
Statement: The recurrence CLI does not create rules automatically from detection — detection only prints proposals; rule creation always requires the explicit user approval of the seeded field loop (or fully-flagged add).

Rationale: The docstrings state it explicitly ('NOTHING is created'; 'the proposal alone never creates a rule') — recurring money movement is trusted only to a human-reviewed rule. Evidence anchors: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:855-857 and 915-918.

docs.title: non-goal:4
docs.text:
Statement: The ledger TUI does no offset/scroll math for cursor movement or dialogs — the DataTable clamps at the first/last row and auto-scrolls the viewport itself by row; only the initial projection-anchor positioning uses line-based scroll math (rows are mixed-height, so that one case needs line offsets).

Rationale: Stated verbatim in the module docstring ('The DataTable clamps at the first/last row by itself (no offset math here)… only the initial-position scroll math needs line offsets') and honored by the code: _focus_row and _position_at are the only scroll computations, both called with call_after_refresh.

docs.title: non-goal:5
docs.text:
Statement: Groups are not journaled and never move money: the projection hides members and rolls them up at render/walk time only, group add/remove edit only the membership list and leave the member rows untouched in their own stores.

Rationale: Journal = committed money; expected + rules + groups = forecast inputs. Keeping groups outside the journal keeps the committed ledger authoritative and membership reversible.

docs.title: non-goal:6
docs.text:
Statement: Confirm never commits a FUTURE rule instance itself: a future occurrence is handed to recurrence_cli's interactive prefilled prompt walk, and recurrence_cli's own future-date gate refuses an actual dated ahead of today — confirm does not bypass or duplicate that gate.

Rationale: The module reuses recurrence_cli._confirm_instance for future instances (confirm.py:111-113) and its docstring states the gate belongs to recurrence_cli; keeping one date gate avoids two diverging validation paths.

docs.title: non-goal:7
docs.text:
Statement: The reporting layer does no reconciliation or anomaly detection: it renders aggregated totals and balance curves as recorded; it never validates that summed flows match balance deltas (no flag-based or balance-mismatch logic lives in reporting).

Rationale: Balance-mismatch flags exist in the model (FLAG_BALANCE_CHECKING / FLAG_BALANCE_SAVINGS) but reporting only reads balances for display; checking is deferred to other layers.

docs.title: non-goal:8
docs.text: Statement: The journal op vocabulary deliberately has no reconcile operation (nor an opening op): money that moved without a transaction is never silently reconciled — it becomes an explicit correction transaction, listed for owner review. Rationale: Owner policy 2026-09-18: "I will always create a transaction implementing the mutation" — hidden reconciling entries would defeat the journal's auditability, so the maintenance tooling derives explicit correction rows instead.

docs.title: non-goal:9
docs.text: Statement: The maintenance scripts do not silently destroy superseded data: retired stores are preserved (timestamped .retired backups), refused rows are always reported for owner decision, and nothing is ever guessed away. Rationale: None

docs.title: quirk:1 (lineage)
docs.text:
Description: remint() is a repair pass kept in the core module: it re-mints the ids of journal rows whose stored id no longer matches their content hash — a legacy of a 2026-09-19 writer bug where ts was written into the line but the id was minted before ts became hashed content (four live observer rows). Only affected lines are rewritten, byte-preserving the rest; a dry_run mode reports without writing. It exists so old journals stay foldable under the current hashing rules.

Parity Relevance: A parity implementation must decide whether remint's repair semantics (re-derived ids, line-level rewrite, dry_run report shape) are normative or historical-only; replaying the same legacy journal must produce the same repaired ids either way. Impact: src/financials/journal.py:413-446

docs.title: quirk:10 (integrity)
docs.text:
Description: _resolve_ledger_target matches a fix id as 'full hash id OR t.id.startswith(fix_id)' — a prefix match, not a word-boundary match. A fix id that is a prefix of another transaction's id does not merely risk ambiguity: _load_fixes_file and the fix-file format invite hand-written short ids, where full-hash vs short-prefix is indistinguishable. Ambiguity raises only when MORE THAN ONE row matches; a unique prefix silently wins, and a one-character prefix of a unique hash is a legal target.

Parity Relevance: Parity fixtures should use full hash ids; a single-char prefix may resolve to a different row in a different dataset and silently apply the fix to the wrong transaction. Impact: src/financials/fixes.py:61-69

docs.title: quirk:11 (parity)
docs.text:
Description: fixes.py defines and exports GLOBAL_OPS = {'remove_row', 'add_expected_row', …} in all, but no other file or symbol references it. It is a vestige of the pre-journal global-op engine: the journaled change-set now refuses global ops outright (fix_id 'all' raises ValueError in both apply_ops and apply_field_ops).

Parity Relevance: Parity work should not reproduce the GLOBAL_OPS export surface; the live behavior is that global ops are refused, not dispatched. Impact: src/financials/fixes.py:55, src/financials/fixes.py:274

docs.title: quirk:12 (parity)
docs.text:
Description: Monthly and yearly expansion silently skips impossible calendar dates: when the rule's day does not exist in a month (day 31 in a 30-day month, Feb 29 in non-leap years), push() swallows the ValueError and that month produces no occurrence; the next month resumes normally. No error, warning, or substitute date is emitted, and monthly rules default to day 1, yearly to month 1/day 1, when unset — the "one instance per month" reading of a rule is subtly false for day-29/30/31 rules.

Parity Relevance: Any parity reimplementation must reproduce the exact skip-not-shift behavior; shifting to the next valid date instead would change which months expand and alter both virtual ids and coverage windows. Impact: src/financials/recurrences.py:69-89

docs.title: quirk:13 (forecast)
docs.text:
Description: Tier B detection deliberately has NO magnitude guardrail: budget-style series (the owner confirms a fixed budget with the actual spend) vary far more than 2x between occurrences, so rejecting large spreads would kill real patterns; instead the observed [min, max] spread is surfaced honestly as amount_range on the proposal. The trade-off is accepted because proposals are review-only — a noisy proposal costs a glance, not an automatic rule.

Parity Relevance: A parity implementation adding an intuitive "amounts differ too much" rejection would diverge: proposals the reference detector emits must keep being emitted even with wild amount spreads, as long as dates classify and signs are uniform. Impact: src/financials/recurrences.py:236-239

docs.title: quirk:14 (naming)
docs.text:
Description: RETRY_LIMIT = 3 is defined at module level (line 42) but never used anywhere in the file — it reads like a leftover from an earlier retry prompt design. Everything else in the module is wired; this is the only dead symbol in the covers.

Parity Relevance: Harmless for parity, but a parity port that treats it as meaningful retry behavior would invent behavior that does not exist. Impact: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:42

docs.title: quirk:15 (format)
docs.text:
Description: The weekly cadence confirmation after a successful add prints a doubled opening parenthesis — 'wekelijks ((ma))' — for frequency weekly, while the biweekly branch prints the single-paren form 'tweewekelijks (ma)'. A cosmetic format slip in the success message, not the data.

Parity Relevance: A parity harness diffing success-line output would flag 'wekelijks ((ma))' as a mismatch; the doubled paren is in the reference output, not a bug to fix away. Impact: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:469-472

docs.title: quirk:16 (forecast)
docs.text:
Description: Projection windows are hard-coded in multiple shapes: _next_instances scans in 400-day chunks (window_end = TODAY() + 400 days), _find_instance projects through today + 400 days, and the lookback uses RULE_LOOKBACK_DAYS from the engine module. The 400-day forward horizon is a magic number, not a named constant; it silently bounds how far 'komende' dates and instance resolution can reach.

Parity Relevance: A parity port must reproduce the 400-day horizon to match projected instance lists and confirm/edit resolvability for far-future instances. Impact: src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:75-77, src/financials/recurrence_cli.py:590

docs.title: quirk:17 (lineage)
docs.text:
Description: The view layer hosts the canonical-journal boot (command_journal), whose docstring still speaks of a pre-promotion migration staging journal: a one-time data-migration mechanism lives on inside the view composition path used by every view command and the projection spine, long after the migration itself.

Parity Relevance: A parity port may not realize the view boot is promotion-aware; porting only the data-journal boot would break environments that still have the migration staging journal. Impact: src/financials/ledger_view.py:37-51

docs.title: quirk:18 (format)
docs.text:
Description: _fmt renders amounts in a Dutch-style format by round-tripping the thousands separator: f"{value:,.2f}" then replacing commas with X, dots with commas and X back with dots (line 96-99). The byte-exact output and the '—' em-dash for None values are part of rendered table text.

Parity Relevance: Byte-parity on rendered tables requires reproducing this exact separator dance and the em-dash placeholder; a locale-aware formatter will not match. Impact: src/financials/ledger_view.py:96-99

docs.title: sensitivity:1
docs.text:
Boot-time corruption policy splits responsibilities: content-hash mismatches in either journal rows or checkpoint rows are refused loudly (ValueError), truncation/reordering is explicitly NOT the hash's job — a checkpoint tip that never appears in the journal refuses boot with a message deferring structural damage to "the tip + backup path". The checkpoint's failure direction is always replayable (journal ahead of checkpoint), never silent data loss.

Found in: src/financials/journal.py:483-488, src/financials/journal.py:526-531, src/financials/journal.py:450-458

docs.title: sensitivity:10
docs.text:
The add dialog bypasses entry._validate's future-date rejection by dispatching to add_expected BEFORE calling _validate for past dates. Any refactor that reorders _submit's steps would push future-dated rows into the journal path and let _validate reject them (or worse, break dispatch parity) — the ordering between dispatch and validation is the load-bearing detail, mirroring the CLI's own dispatch-before-validate order.

Found in: src/financials/tui/add.py:332-364

docs.title: sensitivity:11
docs.text:
The TUI add screen imports the CLI's private validation internals (_validate, _validate_amount from financials.entry) as its rules source of truth. Renames/signature changes of those underscore-private functions break the dialog silently at import time; conversely, the dialog is the place where those rules must be kept visible — inline error text is TUI-specific but the RULES must never be duplicated locally.

Found in: src/financials/tui/add.py:51-54, src/financials/tui/add.py:326-337

docs.title: sensitivity:12
docs.text:
The last-resort member resolver recomputes recurrence expansion over a wide window (lookback + 60 days past, 400 days future) and re-hashes each active rule's instances to match a dangling member id — content hashes make instance ids edit-sensitive: a rule edit re-mints ids, so group membership silently references stale ids and resolution drifts onto whichever rule instance currently hashes to that id.

Found in: src/financials/groups.py:143-157, src/financials/groups.py:167-178

docs.title: sensitivity:13
docs.text:
_render_show excludes dangling members from the rollup total but still shows them listed as dangling; a group whose members are all dangling exits 2 — so a stale-id membership (e.g. after a recurrence rule edit) degrades quietly into a wrong/empty total rather than failing loudly.

Found in: src/financials/groups.py:216-249

docs.title: sensitivity:14
docs.text: Group confirm mutates the mutable membership file while iterating members: it reloads load_groups() after each save and re-finds the group before re-pointing a retired e-id. An interrupted run leaves a partially-confirmed group whose remaining e-members are stale; the idempotent re-run path depends on "is al actual — niets te doen" so already-committed members are skipped without harm. Any parity port must preserve this re-resolve-on-every-save discipline or risk re-pointing against a stale group copy. Found in: src/financials/confirm.py:161-170

docs.title: sensitivity:15
docs.text:
find_entry is a regression-sensitive resolver: an e-id once resolved to an actual row while remove_row routed by prefix, deleting the other store's row; the strict prefix scoping (e-prefix => expected-only, return None on miss) protects against cross-store deletion and must not be relaxed to a global id search.

Found in: src/financials/model.py:98-116

docs.title: sensitivity:16
docs.text:
APPROVED_CATEGORIES in model.py is computed once at import time from the config; code reading model.APPROVED_CATEGORIES sees a stale snapshot if config changes at runtime, while ask._sorted_categories deliberately re-reads config per call — consumers must be consistent about which source of truth they use.

docs.title: sensitivity:17
docs.text:
The report row filter matches "summary row" as a substring of the note (not an equality check on the marker constant), so any note containing that phrase excludes a row from ALL flow figures and category rankings — an over-matching exclusion sensitive to note text drift.

Found in: src/financials/reporting.py:59, src/financials/model.py:44

docs.title: sensitivity:18
docs.text:
Mutation ids are content hashes: the journal's integrity depends on every row's id equaling the hash of its own content. Repairing ids means rewriting immutable-looking journal rows in place — any tooling that assumes journal rows are write-once must be coordinated with this repair script (backup + fold verification included here).

# src/financials/journal.py — lines 386–410
def fold(source: Journal | Path | str) -> tuple[Ledger, str]:
  """THE canonical fold (roadmap step 3): replay a journal into a ledger,
  returning (ledger, tip).

  Entries are positioned by DATE (the engine's date-positioned insert —
  the canonical checkpoint fold, decided 2026-09-21; the bootstrap's
  file-order fold stays the one-time evidence pass inside the script).
  The tip is the last APPLIED mutation in JOURNAL order — entry order
  and journal order are independent. Every row is rehash-verified
  BEFORE it is applied: the id IS the row's anti-corruption validator,
  so a tampered row stops the fold loudly instead of silently producing
  a wrong checkpoint."""

  journal = source if isinstance(source, Journal) else Journal(source)
  ledger = Ledger()
  tip = ""
  for mutation in journal:
    if mutation.id and mutation.content_hash != mutation.id:
      raise ValueError(
        f"journal row {mutation.id!r} fails its content hash "
        f"(rehashed {mutation.content_hash}) — refusing to fold a corrupt journal: {mutation}"
      )
    ledger.apply(mutation)
    tip = mutation.id or tip
  return ledger, tip

  def fit_columns(self) -> None:
    """Layout: every column except the merged Transactie column keeps
    its content width (Datum included — it must count against the
    budget, else the total overflows the viewport and the last column
    is pushed out of sight); the merged column takes every remaining
    cell so the numeric columns end flush at the right edge. DataTable
    has no flex columns — mechanism: pin the fixed columns' widths,
    size the merged column against the table's scrollable width (never
    below its content width), and refit virtual_size."""
    if not self.columns:
      return
    columns = self.ordered_columns
    entry_col = columns[1]
    used = 0
    for col in columns:
      if col is entry_col:
        continue
      col.auto_width = False
      col.width = col.content_width
      used += col.get_render_width(self)
    entry_col.auto_width = False
    # avail already includes the entry column's 2×cell_padding share
    # (every get_render_width carries it) — subtract it so the total
    # render width equals the viewport exactly and no horizontal
    # scrollbar appears.
    entry_col.width = max(
      self.scrollable_content_region.width - used - 2 * self.cell_padding,
      entry_col.content_width,
    )
    self.virtual_size = Size(
      entry_col.get_render_width(self) + used, self.virtual_size.height
    )
    self.scroll_x = 0.0

def remint(source: Journal | Path | str, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
  """Re-mint the ids of rows whose stored id does not match their content
  hash (repair for the 2026-09-19 writer bug: ts was written into the
  line but the id was minted before ts was hashed content — four live
  observer rows).

  Only the affected lines are rewritten (byte-preserving everything
  else); the content itself is never touched — the id doubles as the
  anti-corruption validator, so a re-mint re-derives it from the row's
  own content. Returns the repaired rows as (line number, old id, new
  id). Dry-run reports without writing."""
  journal = source if isinstance(source, Journal) else Journal(source)
  path = journal.path
  lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
  repaired: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []
  for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
    if not line.strip():
      continue
    properties = json.loads(line)
    op = properties.pop("op", None)
    cls = Journal.MUTATIONS.get(op)
    if cls is None:
      raise NotImplementedError(f"mutation op {op!r} is not implemented")
    mutation = cls(**properties)
    if mutation.id and mutation.content_hash != mutation.id:
      new_id = mutation.content_hash
      properties["id"] = new_id
      properties["op"] = op
      ordered = {key: properties[key] for key in sorted(properties)}
      lines[number - 1] = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
      repaired.append((number, mutation.id, new_id))
  if repaired and not dry_run:
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
  return repaired

docs.title: Sensitivity Statement
docs.text: Boot-time corruption policy splits responsibilities: content-hash mismatches in either journal rows or checkpoint rows are refused loudly (ValueError), truncation/reordering is explicitly NOT the hash's job — a checkpoint tip that never appears in the journal refuses boot with a message deferring structural damage to "the tip + backup path". The checkpoint's failure direction is always replayable (journal ahead of checkpoint), never silent data loss.

docs.text: The last-resort member resolver recomputes recurrence expansion over a wide window (lookback + 60 days past, 400 days future) and re-hashes each active rule's instances to match a dangling member id — content hashes make instance ids edit-sensitive: a rule edit re-mints ids, so group membership silently references stale ids and resolution drifts onto whichever rule instance currently hashes to that id.

def _rule_dates(rule) -> list[date]:
  """All expansion dates of an active rule over a wide window (past
  60 days through +400 days — the same breadth as the view's walk plus
  the instance resolver's future reach)."""
  from financials.recurrences import RULE_LOOKBACK_DAYS, _instances_for

  today = date.today()
  return _instances_for(
    rule,
    today - timedelta(days=RULE_LOOKBACK_DAYS + 60),
    today + timedelta(days=400),
  )

def _render_show(group: Group) -> int:
  rows: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = []

  for column, justify in (

    ("Categorie", "left"),
    ("Bedrag", "right"),
  ):
    table.add_column(column, justify=justify)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
  for row in rows:
    table.add_row(*row)

docs.text: Group confirm mutates the mutable membership file while iterating members: it reloads load_groups() after each save and re-finds the group before re-pointing a retired e-id. An interrupted run leaves a partially-confirmed group whose remaining e-members are stale; the idempotent re-run path depends on "is al actual — niets te doen" so already-committed members are skipped without harm. Any parity port must preserve this re-resolve-on-every-save discipline or risk re-pointing against a stale group copy.

docs.text: find_entry is a regression-sensitive resolver: an e-id once resolved to an actual row while remove_row routed by prefix, deleting the other store's row; the strict prefix scoping (e-prefix => expected-only, return None on miss) protects against cross-store deletion and must not be relaxed to a global id search.

# src/financials/model.py — lines 98–116
def find_entry(
  entry_id: str, transactions: list[Transaction], expected: list[Transaction]
) -> Transaction | None:
  """Resolve an id within the provided stores — prefix-scoped: t####
  searches the actual register only, e#### the expected register only
  (the documented id contract; regression: an e-id colliding with an
  actual row used to resolve to the actual row while remove_row routed
  by prefix, deleting the other store's row). Committed rows resolve in
  the LEDGER (ledger.find); this helper is for the expected register and
  callers holding explicit lists. None when absent."""
  if entry_id.startswith("e") and entry_id[1:].isdigit():
    for t in expected:
      if t.id == entry_id:
        return t
    return None
  for t in transactions:
    if t.id == entry_id:
      return t
  return None

docs.text: Mutation ids are content hashes: the journal's integrity depends on every row's id equaling the hash of its own content. def projected_checking(
  ledger: Ledger, iso_date: str, amount: float
) -> tuple[float | None, Transaction | None]:
  """The projected checking balance for an entry of `amount` dated
  iso_date, chaining from the ledger's date-positioned predecessor (the
  engine's find_parent — the same row the fold will chain from). Returns
  (projection, predecessor); (None, None) when no predecessor exists."""
  from financials.journal import Ledger as _Ledger  # noqa: F401 — typing

  parent, _idx = ledger.find_parent(Date(iso_date))
  if parent is None:
    return None, None
  projected = round(parent.balances.get("checking", 0.0) + amount, 2)
  return projected, parent

docs.text: Overdracht (transfer) bookings touch two accounts in one mutation (checking and the savings mirror). Every interactive path that creates, edits-in-place, moves, or deletes an Overdracht row warns the user that the booking also affects the savings chain and to check 'financials list'. The change-set engine mirrors this twice: replace_field maintains the 'savings' = -amount mirror posting on amount fixes for Overdracht rows, and _project_transaction feeds the paired postings verbatim into UpdateMutation. Any mutation path that forgets the mirror posting silently corrupts the savings balance chain.

def replace_field(target: LedgerTransaction, field: str, value) -> LedgerTransaction:
  """The row with one field replaced (the update's final state)."""
  from dataclasses import replace as _replace

  if field == "amount":
    postings = dict(target.postings)
    postings["checking"] = round(value, 2)
    if target.category == "Overdracht":
      postings["savings"] = round(-value, 2)
    return _replace(target, postings=postings)
  if field in {"date", "description", "category"}:
    return _replace(target, **{field: value})
  raise ValueError(f"unsupported field for ledger fix: {field!r}")

def commit_instance(
  rule_hit: Recurrence,
  occurrence_date: date,
  confirmed_date: date,
  description: str,
  category: str,
  amount: float,
) -> int:
  """The no-prompt commit core shared by `_confirm_instance` (the values
  come from the prefilled prompts) and `confirm.py` (the values come from
  the rule itself): one AddMutation — the journal records committed money;
  the instance is virtual. When the committed row does NOT cover the
  rule's period (drifted amount or out-of-window date), the occurrence is
  recorded as an exception so the unconfirmed instance doesn't linger in
  OPEN; a covering commit supersedes it automatically (nothing to
  record)."""
  from financials.commands import cmd_add

  iso = occurrence_date.isoformat()
  journal = command_journal()
  _mutation, entry = cmd_add(
    iso_date=confirmed_date.isoformat(),
    description=description,
    category=category,
    amount=amount,
    journal=journal,
  )
  if entry is None:
    console.print("[red]Niet bevestigd: de boeking kon niet worden toegepast.[/red]")
    return 2
  # No ghost instance: a commit that covers the rule's period supersedes
  # it in the projection; a drifted commit (amount/date outside the
  # superseding window) is excepted so the instance leaves OPEN.
  covered = (
    category == rule_hit.category
    and abs(amount - rule_hit.amount) <= AMOUNT_TOLERANCE
    and abs((confirmed_date - occurrence_date).days) <= DAY_WINDOW
  )
  if not covered:
    rules = load_recurrences()
    for rule in rules:
      if rule.description == rule_hit.description and rule.category == rule_hit.category:
        rule.exceptions = sorted(set(rule.exceptions) | {iso})
    save_recurrences(rules)
  balances = entry.balances
  console.print(
    f"[green]Bevestigd: {iso} → {entry.id}[/green]  [dim]checking "
    f"{balances.get('checking', 0.0):,.2f}, spaar "
    f"{balances.get('savings', 0.0):,.2f}[/dim]"
  )

def open_rows(today: date | None = None) -> list[Transaction]:
  """The OPEN section's rows (the `confirm` picker's backlog): every
  projected row dated on or before today — overdue expected entries plus
  landed-but-unconfirmed rule instances. A view-level read: nothing
  writes stores."""
  walk, _anchor = _projection_walk(today or date.today())
  iso_today = (today or date.today()).isoformat()
  return [t for t, _c, _s in walk if t.date <= iso_today]

  def fit_columns(self) -> None:
    """Layout: every column except the merged Transactie column keeps
    its content width (Datum included — it must count against the
    budget, else the total overflows the viewport and the last column
    is pushed out of sight); the merged column takes every remaining
    cell so the numeric columns end flush at the right edge. DataTable
    has no flex columns — mechanism: pin the fixed columns' widths,
    size the merged column against the table's scrollable width (never
    below its content width), and refit virtual_size."""
    if not self.columns:
      return
    columns = self.ordered_columns
    entry_col = columns[1]
    used = 0
    for col in columns:
      if col is entry_col:
        continue
      col.auto_width = False
      col.width = col.content_width
      used += col.get_render_width(self)
    entry_col.auto_width = False
    # avail already includes the entry column's 2×cell_padding share
    # (every get_render_width carries it) — subtract it so the total
    # render width equals the viewport exactly and no horizontal
    # scrollbar appears.
    entry_col.width = max(
      self.scrollable_content_region.width - used - 2 * self.cell_padding,
      entry_col.content_width,
    )
    self.virtual_size = Size(
      entry_col.get_render_width(self) + used, self.virtual_size.height
    )
    self.scroll_x = 0.0

    table.call_after_refresh(table.fit_columns)

docs.title: Sensitivity Statement
docs.text: _load_view calls build_view with project=0 and projection_horizon=date(today.year, 12, 31) — the TUI bakes in a projection to calendar year end and the footer says so; shifting these composition parameters silently changes which rows render and the anchored scroll position (the projection anchor is derived from sep-projection existing).

  def _load_view(self, focus_id: str | None = None) -> None:
    """(Re)build the composition and render it — on_mount, and after
    every save that changed the ledger (with the cursor re-landed on
    the affected row)."""
    today = self._today or date.today()
    self._window_start = (today - timedelta(days=self._days_back)).isoformat()
    self._view = build_view(
      days=self._days_back,
      project=0,
      days_back=self._days_back,
      projection_horizon=date(today.year, 12, 31),
      today=today,
    )
    assert self._view is not None
    self._fill_table(self._view, focus_id=focus_id)

# src/financials/tui/__init__.py — lines 405–413
  def _initial_anchor_row(table: LedgerTable) -> int:
    """The initial-position anchor row: the PROJECTIE separator's index,
    else the last row (no projection section); 0 on an empty table."""
    if not table.row_count:
      return 0
    try:
      return table.get_row_index("sep-projection")
    except RowDoesNotExist:
      return table.row_count - 1
